Name: Advanced Writing Lives (Online)
About Course: Every day we meet people with interesting life stories.  Our lives are made up of tragic, uplifting and humorous experiences which shape us as individuals.  We love, fight, apologise, account for and endure through whatever comes our way.

Name: Analysing Classical Music: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: The aim of musical analysis is to understand how music exerts such a powerful effect on us. This course introduces some of the main approaches as we attempt to bridge the gap between our intuitions about music and our intellectual knowledge of it.

Name: Animal Behaviour: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Why do animals behave the way they do? In this course we will look at the full range of behaviours found in the animal kingdom, from simple escape behaviours to complex tool use and their evolution.

Name: Britain and Its Empire (Online)
About Course: This course examines the rise and fall of the British Empire and its manifold legacies in Britain and beyond.

Name: Fiction by Victorian Women: George Eliot, Elizabeth Gaskell (Online)
About Course: Some of the great writers of the Victorian period were women. Find out how they portrayed women's issues and lives in such compelling fiction.

Name: Introduction to Philosophy (Online)
About Course: We think we know, but do we? We think we are free, but are we? We think our actions are moral, but are they? What is this reality we take ourselves to live in?  The oldest questions meet the newest technology in this online introduction to philosophy.

Name: Microeconomics: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: This course provides a detailed introduction to microeconomics. On completion of the course, students will have the ability to understand and apply the principles of microeconomics at first-year undergraduate level.

Name: Psychology: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: This course introduces the science of psychology, exploring the richness of human functions, uncovering the brain's secrets and revealing its complexities. Studies from biological, psychodynamic, cognitive, behavioural and social approaches are presented.

Name: What is Local History?
About Course: The course introduces students to approaches, methods and sources for English local history, with an emphasis on the documentary evidence available for studying manors, parishes, towns and populations.

Name: Ancient Egypt: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: From royal pyramids, court artisans and powerful pharaohs, to grandiose temples, mysterious gods and foreign invasions, participants will experience the world of ancient Egypt, its highs and lows, and the rich tapestry of its culture.

Name: Churchill: Soldier, Politician and Statesman (Online)
About Course: Sir Winston Churchill, regarded as one of Britain's greatest statesmen, still provokes controversy and debate. The aim of this course is to study his life in detail, assess his successes and failures and to gain some insights into the complex personality.

Name: Critical Reading (Online)
About Course: This course is for anyone who would like to learn to read beneath the surface, pay attention to language and form, and become a critical reader.

Name: Getting Started in Creative Writing (Online)
About Course: This course introduces the key characteristics of creative writing. You will be supported with stage-by-stage guidance as you assimilate and employ a range of critical and creative methods. The course includes tutor feedback and participant discussion.

Name: Literary Theory: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Although literary theory might sometimes seem intimidating, it can be very accessible and exciting. This course aims to demystify literary theory, showing how it illuminates literary texts and enriches our understanding and enjoyment of literature.

Name: Middle English Literature (Online)
About Course: Middle English literature is not all prayer and piety and men in armour. Find a rich cultural heritage in Middle English poems, plays and prose.

Name: Philosophy of Religion (Online)
About Course: The course looks at what, if anything, it is that Jews, Christians and Muslims are agreeing about when they claim that there is a God; and we shall look at what, if any, prospects there are for rationally defending or attacking this claim.

Name: Social Entrepreneurship (Online)
About Course: Students on this course will gain knowledge about social entrepreneurs, and how to develop creative solutions to address social problems utilising Gandhi's model of 'be the change you wish to see in the world' to make a difference in the lives of others.

Name: Art Nouveau across Europe (Online)
About Course: From Paris to Moscow, Glasgow to Barcelona, this course examines the richness and variety of European art nouveau.

Name: Civil War and Revolution: Britain Divided, 1640-1660 (Online)
About Course: The civil wars that swept across the British Isles in the 17th century left few lives untouched. This course will explore the causes, conduct and significance of the English civil wars.

Name: Exploring the Universe (Online)
About Course: How old is the universe? How unusual is the Solar System? How will it all end? Oxford astronomers Chris Lintott and Robert Simpson provide an overview of the last 13.7 billion years of cosmic evolution, answering these questions and more.

Name: Globalisation (Online)
About Course: Everybody is talking about 'globalisation' - but what does it really mean? What factors drive globalisation and what are the consequences for all of us? How can and should we govern processes of globalisation?

Name: Henry VIII (Online)
About Course: The reign of Henry VIII transformed British history. This course charts the political, religious and cultural changes of the period.

Name: Jane Austen (Online)
About Course: Many readers enjoy Austen's novels, but what makes them so special and enduring?

Name: Learning to Look at Modern Art (Online)
About Course: This course will seek to provide guidelines about how to look at modern art in an open-minded, critical and analytical way.

Name: Learning to Look at the Visual Arts (Online)
About Course: This course offers you the opportunity to learn how to study and analyse paintings, drawings and prints, and learn the 'language of looking'.

Name: Origins of Human Behaviour (Online)
About Course: What makes humans different from other primates? When did we become human? This course will chart the development of human behaviour.

Name: Public Policy Economics (Online)
About Course: All of us are affected by government policies, and governments place particular emphasis on economic policies. This course will equip you to evaluate the economic arguments made about public policy choices.

Name: Ritual and Religion in Prehistory (Online)
About Course: How can we begin to understand the spiritual lives of prehistoric people? When do religious ideologies first appear on the human evolutionary timescale? Using both anthropology and archaeological evidence these and many other questions are examined.

Name: Social Anthropology: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Social anthropology is the study of how humans give meaning to the world through different social norms, values, practices and means of organisation. This course provides an exciting and dynamic introduction to the world of social anthropology.

Name: The Wars of The Roses: Power, Politics and Personalities (Online)
About Course: The recent discovery of Richard III's remains in Leicester highlights the dynamic new research being conducted into the period known as the Wars of the Roses. This course asks students to engage with the latest work on this exciting and tumultuous period.

Name: Theory of Knowledge (Online)
About Course: The theory of knowledge is one of the most central areas of philosophy. In this online course you will cover the key issues in epistemology while also learning to think for yourself and develop your own answers to the core questions in this area.

Name: Mapping the Spatial Structure of Historic Cities
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Professional development- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Delve into historic urban landscapes, mastering spatial analysis techniques in this 2-day course. Uncover layers of history and culture, enriching your professional skill set. Learn how the layout of cities helps to shape movement, interaction and trade.

Name: Academic Literacy: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: If you are new to higher education, or have not studied for some time, you may find it useful to brush up your reading, note-making and essay-writing skills, and to revisit the basic rules of punctuation and grammar.

Name: Brontës (Online)
About Course: How did three sisters living apparently secluded, eventless lives write such original, passionate and dramatic literature?

Name: Contemporary British Fiction (Online)
About Course: If you have ever been daunted by terms such as 'modernism', 'magic realism' or 'postmodern', this is the course for you.

Name: Ethics: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: In this introduction to ethics, we shall examine four important ethical theories, applying them to two practical questions: the rights of animals and euthanasia. There will be plenty of opportunity to engage in debate and test your own thinking.

Name: Inequality and Labour Markets (Online)
About Course: Labour market inequality is a defining issue of the 21st century. This course examines the effect of globalisation and technology on inequality, and what we can do to reduce it.

Name: Investigating the Elizabethans (Online)
About Course: The Elizabethan world witnessed some of the most momentous and memorable events in English history. Investigate the experiences and reactions of individuals to these changes, events and issues.

Name: Islamic Art and Architecture (Online)
About Course: This course is for anyone interested in understanding Islamic art and culture, and examines the relationship between faith and art forms.

Name: Philosophy of Science (Online)
About Course: This course introduces key issues in the philosophy of science, including debates about the nature of the scientific method, theories of confirmation, the demarcation of science from non-science, the rationality of theory change, and scientific realism.

Name: Political Philosophy: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Political philosophy contains some of the greatest writings in the Western intellectual tradition. This online course introduces you to the central questions concerning the state, by means of classical and contemporary texts.

Name: Shakespeare (Online)
About Course: This course focuses on five Shakespeare plays, covering a range of genres and periods of his writing.

Name: Western Architecture: The Modern Era (Online)
About Course: Beginning with the vital structural innovations of the late Victorian era, this course traces the rise and spread of modernism in European and American architecture, and concludes by examining contemporary architecture and future possibilities.

Name: Writing Fiction for Young Adults (Online)
About Course: Find your own voice and your own niche in writing for young adults, in sub-genres from realism to the supernatural.

Name: Van Gogh Today
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: On the occasion of the National Gallery’s upcoming exhibition 'Vincent Van Gogh: Poets and Lovers', we will consider the enduring interest of this painter and how his relevance is being framed anew.

Name: Machine Learning of Wearables in Large Scale Biomedical Studies
About Course: A residential short course on machine learning of wearables datasets, connecting post-graduate and post-doctoral researchers from academia and industry with experts at Oxford's Big Data Institute and Nuffield Department of Population Health.

Name: Ancestral Voices: The Earliest English Literature (Online)
About Course: This course introduces you to Old English literature: from tales of heroism, courage and fellowship, to poignant elegies of love and loss.

Name: Artificial Intelligence Concepts: Introduction to Machine Learning (Online)
About Course: Machine Learning methods lie at the heart of the Artificial Intelligence revolution. This course introduces fundamental concepts to explain Machine Learning methods, potential, and pitfalls to a general audience.

Name: Critical Reasoning: A Romp through the Foothills of Logic (Online)
About Course: Reasoning enables us to acquire knowledge, to persuade others and to evaluate their arguments. But only if we reason well. We shall be learning how to recognise, evaluate, construct and analyse arguments, and how to recognise common fallacies.

Name: Europe of the Dictators (Online)
About Course: Why were the inter-war years a period of such political extremism and dictatorial rule across Europe?

Name: Financial Investment Principles (online)
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: This online course will provide you with a thorough introduction to finance, financial markets and how financial markets interact with the wider economy.

Name: International Labour Migration: Economics, Politics and Ethics (Online)
About Course: This global course analyses one of the most controversial public policy issues of the 21st century: how to regulate international labour migration and the rights of migrant workers.

Name: Reality, Being and Existence: An Introduction to Metaphysics (Online)
About Course: An introduction to metaphysics, the most general investigation of reality. It has been at the centre of philosophy since the beginning of the Western tradition in ancient Greece, and many of its concerns are the same as those of Plato and Aristotle.

Name: The Architecture of the English Medieval Cathedral (Online)
About Course: This course will explore the English medieval cathedral as a developing institution which survived over a thousand years of religious upheaval and historical change, focusing on the multifaceted architecture of a range of truly great churches.

Name: The History of Economic Thought (Online)
About Course: This course evaluates the development of economic thought through the eyes of Greek, Chinese, Indian and European traditions before exploring economic thought in the context of the 20th century.

Name: The Making of Modern Britain (Online)
About Course: A modern, democratic, multicultural Britain developed throughout the twentieth century. This course will examine the key social, economic and political influences that have shaped modern Britain.

Name: Who are the Celts? (Online)
About Course: What do we really know about the Celtic world? These ancient communities left us  captivating artefacts and imposing earthworks, but also with more subtle clues from which we can tease out the origins of the peoples who have come to be known as the Celts.

Name: Managing Workplace Behaviour for Better Performance (online)
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: Learn how to make the work system work and explore the ways in which you can create a more successful physical and psychological workplace.

Name: Understanding the Self: Personality Theories
About Course: Who am I? Why am I this way? Why do I make certain choices? Can I change? This online day school presents the main psychological theories of personality and explains how psychologists measure it.

Name: Artificial Intelligence Concepts: Practical Applications (Online)
About Course: Understanding the impact of Artificial Intelligence, now and in the future, is a key skill in the knowledge economy. This course develops a critical understanding of real-world AI applications by introducing various case studies to a general audience.

Name: Bioethics for Beginners (Online)
About Course: Do you think reproductive cloning is morally permissible? Do you check food labels to exclude buying any with GM ingredients? Would you worry if the government introduced compulsory depositing of DNA in the national DNA bank?

Name: Elizabeth I (Online)
About Course: This course will examine the life and reign of Elizabeth I, from her troubled childhood to the death of the aged Virgin Queen. But what do we really know of this iconic queen? Can her reign be accounted a success?

Name: English Landscape Gardens: 1650 to the Present Day (Online)
About Course: This course is the ideal introduction to English garden history. It provides an overview of five centuries of development, from baroque formalism through the naturalistic landscape style, right up to contemporary cutting-edge planting style.

Name: English Poetry of the First World War (Online)
About Course: Some of the most powerful and moving English poetry of the modern period was written during or about the First World War.

Name: Inter-culturally Speaking (Online)
About Course: Are we just who we think we are, or are we also who others think we are? Are we born prejudiced? Can we talk of 'national characteristics'? How can we best live together on this planet?

Name: Italian Renaissance Art c.1400-c.1600 (Online)
About Course: From Bellini and Botticelli to tapestry and tableware, the material culture of the Italian Renaissance continues to fascinate us to this day. This course is an opportunity to explore this unique period.

Name: Learning to Look at Western Architecture (Online)
About Course: This course is designed to enable you to 'read' the architecture of the Western world in a critically informed way.

Name: Minoans and Mycenaeans (Online)
About Course: The Minoans and Mycenaeans left us with the intriguing Greek Bronze Age sites of Knossos, Mycenae, Pylos and Akrotiri. The excavation of these sites turned archaeologists into superstars, as stunning architecture, sculpture and weaponry were revealed.

Name: The First Civilization: Mesopotamia (Online)
About Course: Civilization was born over 5,000 years ago on the fertile plains of southern Mesopotamia.  Using archaeology and textual sources, this course will build a picture of the Sumerian civilization, one that lies at the root of our own world.

Name: The Modern American Novel: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: In this course we shall study five key novels of the twentieth century - by Fitzgerald, Faulkner, Silko, Morrison and Roth.

Name: Van Eyck to Memling: Northern Renaissance Art c.1430-1480 (Online)
About Course: The work of northern Renaissance artists is often incredibly beautiful, with marvellous colours and textures. But there is much more to their work than simple aesthetics, for it evolved from an intriguing range of religious and cultural beliefs.

Name: Vikings: Raiders, Traders and Settlers (Online)
About Course: Ravagers, despoilers, pagans, the Vikings are often regarded as bloodthirsty pirates. Yet they were also traders, settlers and farmers with a thriving artistic culture and legal systems.  Using archaeology we examine the varied aspects of the Viking world

Name: Britain, France and The Middle East: Colonial Perfidy or 'Civilising Mission'?
About Course: Britain and France have colonised the countries of The Middle East since the mid-19th century, claiming to deliver enlightenment and democracy. However, from the conquest of Algeria to the Sykes-Picot agreement many challenge the integrity of such claims.

Name: Calculus: Introduction
About Course: Calculus is a 'sine qua non' for studying more advanced mathematics, physics, statistics, machine learning and data science. This course will introduce you to the vocabulary and techniques that open the panorama of science and engineering.

Name: Coaching: An Introduction
About Course: This course will help anyone interested in using coaching, whether professionally, as a life skill, or to achieve better results in their work with others. Thought-provoking and practical, this course explores the theory and skills of good coaching.

Name: Collecting Antiquities in Britain: 18th Century to Today
About Course: Dive into the complex history of collecting and exhibiting antiquities in Britain and discover how these eighteenth- and nineteenth-century practices continue to impact us in the present day.

Name: Discover Your Voice
About Course: This course is designed for anyone who would like to sing, but feels that they can't. Through a mixture of seminars and workshops, consideration will be given to various common vocal problems and their solutions.

Name: Foundations of Judaism, Christianity and Islam
About Course: This course is an introduction to foundations of three great world religions: Judaism, Christianity and Islam; their origins and early historical development; their key texts; some of their key beliefs and practices; and the bases of their ethics.

Name: French: Lower Intermediate - Part 1
About Course: Improve your language skills, and understanding of the culture, society and daily life in the French-speaking countries. We will be covering listening, speaking and cultural awareness at lower intermediate level.

Name: Getting Started Writing Your Feature Film Screenplay
About Course: Work actively to understand key screenwriting concepts to build your awareness of the needs of your film idea. Develop this into a riveting outline, populate it with engaging characters, and draw your audience into your story world though genre.

Name: Literature and the Climate Emergency
About Course: This course will explore the capacity of different literary forms, such as speculative fiction, cli-fi, and creative non-fiction, to represent, explore and address climate change and the ‘slow violence’ of the environmental crisis.

Name: Memoir: Begin Writing Your Life
About Course: Everyone has an interesting life story and this course will enable you to present your own.  We shall consider different ways of exploring the life of an individual in ways which recognise each person as unique.

Name: Music Theory: An Introduction
About Course: Explore the basics of classical music theory - notation, rhythm, melody, harmony and form - relating theory to practice with examples from over three centuries of repertoire. Also helpful for those preparing for music theory exams.

Name: Peri to Puccini: The Story of Italian Opera
About Course: Starting with the birth of Italian opera around 1600, this course charts its development through the masterpieces of Monteverdi, Handel, Mozart, Rossini, Donizetti, Bellini, Verdi and Puccini.

Name: Screenwriting: From Film Idea to Pitch
About Course: Actively develop your film idea to build your awareness of its value and needs in this interactive seminar. Expand this into a pitch, communicate what you bring to the story, and why it is worth turning into a film or TV programme.

Name: Technical Team Communication (online)
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: Good communication is key to achieving high performance in the workplace. Technical people need to communicate with multiple stakeholders using multiple communication methods. This course will cover how to excel in written and verbal communication.

Name: The Orthodox Church in the Middle Ages
About Course: Investigating the significant role the Orthodox Church played in the life of the Byzantine Empire, we will discuss its development, spiritual and political power, role in diplomacy, differences with the Church of Rome, and influence on Byzantine art.

Name: The Practice of Magic in Medieval Society
About Course: 'Magic' was a wide-ranging concept that affected many aspects of medieval society. This course will consider the actual and perceived practices of magic in the medieval period and their consequences.

Name: The Rise and Fall of Rome
About Course: This course traces the path of Rome, from a small village in Latium vetus, to an emerging power in Italy, and finally the heart of a Mediterranean Empire, exploring the ecological and socio-political factors that underpin its rise and subsequent fall.

Name: Understanding Emotions
About Course: Explore the definition and history of emotions; the innate/constructed debate; core emotions, positive emotions and psychopathology; provoking their outward expression; role in motivation and behaviour; the connection to wisdom, values, and religion.

Name: World Archaeology
About Course: During this short course, we explore the emergence of fascinating past societies from around the world. Some are mysterious and lost in the mists of time, while others form the foundations of cultural traditions that exist in the world today.

Name: 'The Pencil of Nature’: History of the Art of Photography
About Course: Explore the rich and evolving history of photography, from its earliest origins in Georgian France and England, to the present day. How did photography become established as a serious art form in its own right, and what is its future?

Name: An Archaeology of Natural Places
About Course: An archaeology of natural places offers a nuanced way to engage with human connections to the environmental world and of human cultural expressions about it. Our focus is on European prehistory with global anthropological and ethnographic case studies.

Name: CS50: An Introduction to Computer Science
About Course: Based on the all-conquering Harvard Extension School course, CS50 is now available at Oxford. This course teaches you how to solve problems, both with and without code, with an emphasis on correctness, design, and style.

Name: Chinese (Mandarin): Beginners - Part 1
About Course: Join this interactive course to learn Chinese language and explore its culture. For complete Beginners as well as those who have learnt some Chinese expressions and phrases through travel or socialising.

Name: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT): An Introduction
About Course: An introduction to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy that will enable both experienced clinicians from other therapeutic traditions and people with a general interest in therapy to gain a foundation in key CBT theory and skills.

Name: Counselling Young People: An Introduction
About Course: Exploring the way young people form relationships with themselves and others from a therapeutic perspective. The ten week programme provides transferrable skills and a basic introduction for listening to and helping young people in a variety of settings.

Name: Ethical Capitalism: A Critical Introduction
About Course: What is capitalism? Can it be truly ethical? We address those crucial questions by looking at economic history and theory, as well as sociology and philosophy. We will study the goods and evils of competition, profits, regulation, and growth.

Name: Ethics with Aristotle
About Course: Why engage with an approach to ethics that is 2,300 years old? Because ethics without Aristotle is inconceivable, and his insights into what is good for humans remain invaluable. Join in to explore and discuss the 'Nicomachean Ethics'.

Name: Existential Therapy: An Introduction
About Course: This introduction to Existential Therapy will enable both experienced clinicians from other therapeutic traditions and those with a general interest in therapy to gain a foundation in key existential theory and skills.

Name: Faith for Rights: Empowering Religious Leaders to Protect Human Rights
About Course: This course equips leaders and students with tools from the UN's Faith For Rights framework to merge human rights with faith ideals, fostering cohesive communities. It will be delivered through lectures, sharing of case studies and peer-to-peer learning.

Name: French: Intermediate - Part 1
About Course: Consolidate your proficiency in French language and express your opinions on a range of familiar everyday topics. A progression course for students who completed French: Lower Intermediate - Part 2.

Name: Getting Started in Nature Writing
About Course: Gain an appreciation of different forms of nature writing and produce your own texts in a supportive environment with this online course.

Name: How To Raise Good Citizens? Faith, Philosophy, and Authority
About Course: If we want to avoid the kind of moral catastrophes that marred the 20th Century - from The Holocaust to Pol Pot's Killing Fields - understanding their root causes, and also what might immunise against them, could not be more important.

Name: Increasing Diversity and Inclusion: Women in Leadership (online)
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: This course aims to explore the literature on Women in Leadership and uses an evidence-based approach to explore the journey many women negotiate in moving up the organisational hierarchy.

Name: Modern Legal Controversies
About Course: Judges are 'enemies of the people', covid restrictions 'unacceptable assaults on individual freedom, law 'inadequate to deal with violence against women'. The law has never been so controversial. But what are the realities behind the  headlines?

Name: Poets' Workshop
About Course: If you write poems as a response to life, you shall enjoy this workshop. In a supportive but disciplined group we will help you build on existing ideas and skills and encourage you to discover and explore new possibilities.

Name: Portuguese: Lower Intermediate - Part 1
About Course: Improve your language skills, and understanding of the culture, society and daily life in Portuguese-speaking countries. We will be covering listening, speaking and cultural awareness at lower intermediate level.

Name: Prehistoric Art
About Course: The art of prehistoric Europe is rich with imagery such as cave paintings, carvings, body ornamentation and frescoes. This course considers a range of sites and artefacts in our exploration of the unique and creative ways people visualised their world.

Name: Python Programming for Data Science: Introduction
About Course: Gain insight into the most important programming tools using the Python programming language, for obtaining data, bringing it into a usable form, exploring and modelling it, and for presenting discoveries to a wider audience.

Name: Shakespeare’s Histories
About Course: A study of the English History plays, which deal with the century between the closing years of the reign of Richard II, who was deposed and probably murdered in 1399, and the Battle of Bosworth in 1485, which established the Tudor dynasty.

Name: Spanish: Lower Intermediate - Part 1
About Course: Improve your language skills, and understanding of the culture, society and daily life in the Spanish-speaking countries. We will be covering listening, speaking and cultural awareness at lower intermediate level.

Name: Web Applications Using JavaScript: Introduction
About Course: An introduction to the essentials of web applications: HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Furthermore PHP, MySQL, React, Python's Django which introduce full-stack and cross-platform web application development.

Name: Writing Psychological Thrillers
About Course: A course for aspiring writers of psychological thrillers; whether you are nearly finished or just beginning, these mentor-type sessions will help you gather twisty plots and complex characters into a suspenseful and coherent whole.

Name: Anthropology Applied
About Course: Explore the unique role of applied anthropology in addressing major global challenges of our time. Learn how an integrated understanding of social and cultural dynamics can make the difference between life and death, and change the way you view the world.

Name: Applied Data Science: Introduction
About Course: An intermediate course introducing a blend of data science concepts and technologies in order to enable you to work with everyday data related issues analytically. Gain experience of the entire data science supply chain with a hands-on group project.

Name: Arabic: Beginners - Part 1
About Course: Join this interactive course to learn Arabic language and explore its culture. For complete Beginners as well as those who have learnt some Arabic expressions and phrases through travel or socialising.

Name: Architectural Conservation: History and Global Practice
About Course: Approaches to managing old buildings change across time and between cultures. This course will give historical and global context to architectural conservation practice, and help students broaden their perspective on change in the historic environment.

Name: Architecture and Glass: Stained Glass in English Cathedrals, Medieval to Modern
About Course: Design of stained glass was intertwined with the developing forms of windows and the stone tracery they contained - seen in Canterbury's twelfth century miracles of St Thomas, York's great east window, work by Edward Burne-Jones and Marc Chagall.

Name: Chaos Theory: An Introduction
About Course: An overview of the change of focus from classical physics describing an ideal world to a new approach, modelling nonlinearity and chaotic behaviour. Chaos theory describes a world where the smallest actions might have the greatest consequences.

Name: Critical Thinking: An Introduction
About Course: Discover the fundamental principles of different types of good reasoning. Learn how to identify reliable sources of information. This will make your own thinking more rational and help you analyse and evaluate others' attempts to persuade you.

Name: Economics: Growth or Degrowth?
About Course: Economists and politicians mostly assumed that growth was good. In recent years this has been challenged by environmental activists, ecological economists and eco-socialists. Should society no longer aim for economic growth?

Name: Elgar, Vaughan Williams and the New English Renaissance
About Course: The works of Elgar and Vaughan Williams represent a vibrant resurgence of creativity and innovation in the English musical landscape, inspiring generations of composers, including Holst, Delius and Walton. This course explores their music and legacy.

Name: Exploring Psychology
About Course: In this introduction to Psychology, studies include memory and forgetting, personality, and aspects of childhood development. We will explore human behaviour, and how and why we are unique, using different perspectives from Freud to Positive Psychology.

Name: Film Studies: An Introduction
About Course: This beginners' course will provide a solid introduction to some of the key concepts in film theory. Students will deepen their knowledge of the medium and develop their critical thinking skills through close analysis of films and individual sequences.

Name: Flash Fiction Workshop
About Course: Writing flash fiction brings benefits to writers of all stripes. In this hands-on workshop, we'll be writing each week, discussing our work, and developing new skills in brevity, language and form.

Name: French: Beginners - Part 1
About Course: Join this interactive course to learn French language and explore its culture. For complete Beginners as well as those who have learnt some French expressions and phrases through travel or socialising.

Name: Hegel's Political Philosophy
About Course: Apologist for the Prussian state? Proto-totalitarian? Or liberal? This course will cut through the misconceptions and present Hegel's political philosophy in its full complexity and subtlety, by means of a close reading of his Philosophy of Right (1821).

Name: Infectious Disease Modelling: Applied Methods in R
About Course: Infectious disease modelling utilises data and our understanding of disease biology to provide public health insights. Aimed at a general audience, this course will cover methods for modelling disease transmission in statistical programming language R.

Name: Italian: Beginners - Part 1
About Course: Join this interactive course to learn Italian language and explore its culture. For complete Beginners as well as those who have learnt some Italian expressions and phrases through travel or socialising.

Name: Italian: Lower Intermediate - Part 1
About Course: Improve your language skills, and understanding of the culture, society and daily life in the Italian-speaking countries. We will be covering listening, speaking and cultural awareness at lower intermediate level.

Name: Palaeolithic Art
About Course: Our stone age ancestors have left us a rich legacy of cave art and ornamental objects. This introductory course explores Palaeolithic art from its earliest beginnings to the spectacular artworks created by Upper Palaeolithic modern humans.

Name: Propaganda in the 20th Century
About Course: Propaganda shaped history throughout the world in the twentieth century. We will explore its roots in mass politics, literacy and media, its consequences for democratic and totalitarian politics and culture, and its challenge to the very idea of truth.

Name: R Programming for Data Science: Introduction
About Course: Learn about R programming with this online course. At an introductory level, this course provides you with a solid foundation of the R programming language. Here you will learn the basics of R and gradually move to data processing and manipulation.

Name: Spanish: Intermediate - Part 1
About Course: Consolidate your proficiency in Spanish language and express your opinions on a range of familiar everyday topics. A progression course for students who completed Spanish: Lower Intermediate - Part 2.

Name: The Pianists' Workshop - I
About Course: Explore piano repertoire, interpretation and technique in a lively mixture of talks and workshops, in which all students will have regular opportunities to play. This class is open to players of all levels and you may join the class in any term.

Name: The Victorian Factory Worker
About Course: This course examines the lives and experiences of the Victorian factory worker as well as how Britain's factories changed the world. We will explore what is was really like to work in Britain's factories and how it impacted upon the lives of so many.

Name: Waterloo: A Decisive Victory
About Course: This course will examine Napoleon’s Wars, his abdication and escape, the Campaign of One Hundred Days leading to the epic battle of Waterloo and the far-reaching consequences of that encounter to Europe and beyond.

Name: Writing Fiction: An Introduction
About Course: Want to learn how to write fiction, or hone your skills? This course demystifies the process and craft of fiction writing with many practical tips and tricks. The emphasis is on learning through doing your own writing, in a fun and supportive atmosphere.

Name: Archaeological Survey Using Airborne Lidar
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: Elevate your professional skills with our one-day course. Unlock the potential of recent advances in lidar technology to better understand how you can apply it in your job. Learn how to use and present lidar data for different purposes.

Name: Crime and Punishment in Early Modern London
About Course: Early modern London was viewed as a hotbed of crime & vice, society was thought to be constantly on the verge of crisis. Visitors and locals frequently encountered crime & punishment. This course examines these encounters and the responses they elicited.

Name: Existentialism and Religion
About Course: This course intends to introduce students to existentialist approaches to religious faith and theology. Focusing particularly on human subjectivity rather than dogma, this course seeks to understand what an existential approach to religion involves.

Name: German: Beginners - Part 1
About Course: Join this interactive course to learn German language and explore its culture. For complete Beginners as well as those who have learnt some German expressions and phrases through travel or socialising.

About Course: Improve your language skills, and understanding of the culture, society and daily life in the German-speaking countries. We will be covering listening, speaking and cultural awareness at lower intermediate level.

Name: Global Contemporary Art: An Introduction
About Course: You will be introduced to contemporary art practices from a global perspective, featuring some of the most ground-breaking artists and exhibitions from the 20th and 21st centuries.

Name: Happiness: The State of Mind
About Course: What is happiness? The feeling of joy? An attitude to life? And can we be worthy of happiness? In this course we will explore a range of philosophically interesting questions raised by happiness, reflecting also on the reasons we have for being happy.

Name: Japanese: Lower Intermediate - Part 1
About Course: Improve your language skills, and understanding of the culture, society and daily life in Japanese-speaking countries. We will be covering listening, speaking and cultural awareness at lower intermediate level.

Name: Korean: Beginners - Part 1
About Course: Join this interactive course to learn Korean language and explore its culture. For complete Beginners as well as those who have learnt some Korean expressions and phrases through travel or socialising.

Name: Linear Algebra: Introduction
About Course: Linear algebra and its matrices appear throughout the sciences and in the mathematical parts of the social sciences. This basic course is a prerequisite to understanding advanced mathematics and myriad closely and distantly related quantitative fields.

Name: Plants: How They Grow, Develop and Survive
About Course: How does a plant live? The course will cover aspects of plant life from the cellular to the organismal level, understand how plants are affected by other organisms, and survive in the changing global environment.

Name: Poetry and Place
About Course: This course guides you through inherited literary concepts of 'place' - pastoral, landscape, etc. - before addressing contemporary poetry of an age of rapid travel, forced migration, environmental loss, virtual presence, and the centrality of language.

Name: Portuguese: Beginners - Part 1
About Course: Join this interactive course to learn Portuguese language and explore its culture. For complete Beginners as well as those who have learnt some Portuguese expressions and phrases through travel or socialising.

Name: Reading Literature Critically
About Course: With an emphasis on close critical analysis, this course is designed to enable you to become a more attentive, appreciative and critical reader of literary texts.

Name: Shakespeare in His World
About Course: William Shakespeare's plays are world-famous. But in what kind of world did he live? Through local rivalries, feuding families, legal disputes and high politics, we investigate everyday life in Shakespeare's England.

Name: Should We Do More for the Poor Beyond the Borders?
About Course: Explore the ethical and economic issues arising from an unequal world with borders. Should we focus more on the poorest in the world and less on our fellow citizens? What are the implications for various policies such as trade, aid, tax and immigration?

Name: The Archaeology of the Classical World: An Introduction
About Course: This introductory course introduces the Classical World through an exploration of the archaeology of the cities, villages, temples and daily lives of two ancient Mediterranean societies: the Greeks and the Romans.

Name: The Biochemistry of Metabolic Disorders
About Course: Metabolism is the breakdown of food to provide energy in every cell in the body in order to function properly. Metabolic-related conditions arise from factors such as diet, lack of exercise and genetics leading to disorders such as diabetes and cancer.

Name: The Elements of Musical Composition
About Course: This is a practical course for those interested in composing music of any genre and will concentrate upon the skills common to all composition, focussing this term on melody construction, basic harmony and rhythm.

Name: Writing Characters
About Course: What makes a compelling character, and how do we write one? In this course we'll look at the characters we love and investigate how to breathe life into characterisation in our own work through a series of practical writing exercises and class discussion.

Name: Exploring Planets and Exoplanets: An Introduction to Planetary Sciences
About Course: A conceptual and descriptive exploration of our solar system, and of those around other stars. We will explore the history of planetary discoveries and the exciting prospects for the future, including the search for extraterrestrial life.

Name: Jane Austen and the Development of the Novel Form
About Course: This course explores the six major works of Jane Austen whilst focusing on Northanger Abbey (1817), Emma (1815) and Persuasion (1817). By examining her texts and other sources we investigate how she so innovatively developed the novel as a literary form.

Name: Kafka and Philosophy
About Course: Kafka - beyond the Kafkaesque! A hundred years after Kafka's death, we will read his literary writings and explore their themes, and then assess the interpretations of Kafka provided by philosophers from Walter Benjamin to Jacques Derrida.

Name: Down to Earth: An Introduction to Geology
About Course: An introduction to geology, including plate tectonics, volcanoes, earthquakes and mountains; rocks, minerals and fossils; and the geological history of Britain. You will have a chance to study many real geological specimens.

Name: The Black Hole Information Paradox
About Course: Dive into the Black Hole Information Paradox, a key puzzle in physics where quantum mechanics and general relativity clash, with this day event in Oxford. For enthusiasts and those with a basic understanding of physics.

Name: Down to Earth: An Introduction to Geology
About Course: An introduction to geology, including plate tectonics, volcanoes, earthquakes and mountains; rocks, minerals and fossils; and the geological history of Britain. You will have a chance to study many real geological specimens.

Name: Developing Online Education and Resources
About Course: This fully online course is designed for educators interested in providing flexible learning opportunities,  specifically for health care professionals in a virtual environment.

Name: Introduction to Bionanotechnology

About Course: This five-day course introduces physical scientists, engineers and non-scientists to biological systems and terminology relevant to nanotechnology, and showcases current applications and new developments in bionanotechnology.

Name: Well-Being, Disability and Enhancement
About Course: Central philosophical accounts of well-being, disability and the development of enhanced human capacities, including a debate on whether such technologies lead us to a 'post-human' future.

Name: Clinical Vaccine Development and Biomanufacturing
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: An overview of pre-clinical testing and pathway from pre-clinical testing to field trials, discussions of vaccine immunogenicity, phases of vaccine testing from Phase I to IV, and the development and manufacturing of vaccines with our expert presenters.
Duration: Tue 08 Oct 2024- 11 Oct 2024, See programme details

Name: Fossils and Ancient Life: An Introduction
About Course: Everything you wanted to know about fossils - from the very first life (the 'weird and wonderfuls') to the multitude of life through geological time. The main groups are covered, how they lived, how they died and environmental information they provide.

Name: Non-Destructive Testing for Archaeology and Conservation
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: Join us in Oxford to master non-destructive techniques for built heritage. Get hands-on experience using a range of equipment for assessing archaeology and standing buildings. Learn good practice for informing management and conservation.

Name: Geological Science: An Introduction
About Course: Discover Earth's origin, its chemical composition, continents and oceans, mountains, earthquakes, volcanoes, the history of life, climate change, energy resources, species diversity and natural disasters: geological science explains all these and more.

Name: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT): An Introduction
About Course: An introduction to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy that will enable both experienced clinicians from other therapeutic traditions and people with a general interest in therapy to gain a foundation in key CBT theory and skills.

Name: Positive Psychology
About Course: Positive Psychology offers a direct approach to help people create strategies towards wellbeing. Changing our interpretation of the world can help us feel happier, healthier, more positive, and become more resilient. Learn more at this online workshop.

Name: Death and Devotion: The Art of Death across the Middle Ages
About Course: Uncover the mysteries of the medieval afterlife through its art and architecture. Examine a range of objects from across Western Europe and the Mediterranean.

Name: A Black Theology of Liberation: From Social Death to Black Lives Matter
About Course: Discover the radical legacy of James H. Cone as the grand patriarch of Black theology. Explore the underlying philosophical and theological ideas that have shaped this discipline and form of religious activism.

Name: Green Skills for Everyone
About Course: Are you curious about what ‘sustainability’ and ‘net zero’ mean and how they are relevant to you? Join us for an introduction to the key concepts of climate and sustainability, and to develop green skills for living and working in a changing world

Name: Machine Learning and AI Services on AWS (Amazon Cloud)
About Course: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the largest cloud computing service provider and one of the leaders in machine and deep learning. Learn how to use a collection of their powerful cloud-based machine/deep learning services at this online day school.

Name: The Middle East and Victoria's Women, 1815-1945: Camels, Corsets and Consuls
About Course: Introducing the physical and personal journeys and intercultural collaborations of independent British women as they travelled, and lived, in Ottoman Turkish Arabia and the post-WW1 Middle East at a time of dramatic change (1845-1945).

Name: Introduction to Statistics for Health Care Research
About Course: A flexible online statistics course for busy health and social care professionals who need to understand the basics of health statistics without becoming statisticians.

Name: Practical Steps for Positive Workplaces (online)

About Course: This course provides you with the terminology to identify workplace toxicity. You will learn about psychological tools and techniques to recognise and protect yourself, and be introduced to self-repair strategies to facilitate better mental health.

Name: The Wider Context of Nanotechnology

About Course: A seven-week online course introducing the current state of technology and addressing implications for safety, regulation and innovation. It is for professionals worldwide seeking an overview of this important subject.

Name: Law and the Historic Environment

About Course: Join legal and heritage experts for an intensive 1-day course. If you are responsible for the conservation or investigation of heritage assets, whether in the professional or voluntary sector, this course will help improve your knowledge of the law.

Name: Raiders, Traders and Crusaders: A History of the Baltic Rim
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: The people from the sparse populations and inhospitable lands surrounding the Baltic Sea have played a creative and totally disproportionate role in the history of Europe and the world. This lecture series examines their history and influence

Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Acknowledged to be a relative liberal in domestic policy, Nikita Khrushchev’s foreign policy was a complicated mixture of hard-line repression and conciliatory diplomacy with the US and NATO. This lecture examines the contradictions of ‘co-existence’.

Name: Green and Pleasant Land? 300 Years of British Landscape Art
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Landscape is everywhere: an obvious subject for art which has inspired many of Britain’s greatest painters. This day school explores three centuries of struggle and passion that changed the way we look at the world, from landscape painting to Land Art.

Name: Introduction to Study Skills
About Course: A comprehensive introductory workshop covering time management, reading critically and selectively, taking notes, and planning and writing essays for undergraduate-level study.

Name: Reading the Past: Medieval Handwriting and Palaeography
About Course: Would you like to learn how to read medieval handwriting in original documents? This weekend takes you through the basics of the most common scripts, covering the history of handwriting and taking practical examples from popular record types.

Name: Shops and Shopping: The Architecture of the High Street
About Course: This day school will examine the social role and architectural development of the High Street since its evolution in the 18th century to the development of the chain store in the late 19th century and the retreat of the High Street in the early 21st.

Name: Digital Signal Processing (online)
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: This online course explores DSP concepts and algorithms to develop your understanding of DSP principles and their implementation, equipping you to put ideas into practice and to tackle advanced aspects of DSP.

About Course: Making the move from technical expert to business leader

Name: Neuropsychoanalysis
About Course: An online day school presenting experimental and theoretical information for clinical and experimental psychologists, therapists, counsellors, psychiatrists and other clinicians, taking as a starting point that brain and mind are linked and overlapping.

Name: De Gaulle: Making France Great Again
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: This talk focuses on the maverick foreign policy of Charles de Gaulle, which infuriated both superpowers. While showing military independence from the USA, he was no Soviet apologist, gratuitously insulting communism on a visit to Moscow.

Name: Six Flemish Masters

About Course: Develop your knowledge of human and veterinary vaccinology as we explore all aspects of vaccinology, from Edward Jenner to modern-day vaccines, with state-of-the-art teaching from leading experts.

About Course: An online course for researchers which critically discusses mixed methods approaches to social science analysis.

About Course: What rights do we have over our own bodies? Is it morally acceptable to circumcise young children, perform abortions or compel people to vaccinate? This event with leading philosophers and researchers will explore these and other philosophical puzzles.

About Course: Join us in Oxford for an introduction to a fascinating and turbulent period of English history, viewed through the lens of what people did for fun and leisure.

Name: Literature and Music: From Romanticism to the Jazz Age
About Course: Writers and composers have always influenced one another, in every age. Explore these intertwined influences as the Romantic era gives way to the hedonism of the Jazz age in the aftermath of the First World War.

About Course: A pioneering course that blends the domains of cyber security and artificial intelligence (AI). For existing cyber security professionals who want to understand the impact of AI and also for AI professionals who are interested in cyber security.

About Course: Discover the intricacies of Artificial Intelligence governance, exploring its multifaceted implications for international politics, economics, security, ethics and diplomacy. Join us in Oxford or online.

Name: The Wars of The Roses: Power, Politics and Personalities (Online)

Name: Trollope, Eliot, Dickens and Hardy: Reading Victorian Fiction (Online)

Name: Who are the Celts? (Online)

About Course: Investigate the power of maps and spatial data to document and illustrate local and global issues. Learn how to use Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to explore the world around you and share ideas.

Name: Philosophy of Religion (Online)
About Course: The course looks at what, if anything, it is that Jews, Christians and Muslims are agreeing about when they claim that there is a God; and we shall look at what, if any, prospects there are for rationally defending or attacking this claim.

Name: Social Entrepreneurship (Online)
About Course: Students on this course will gain knowledge about social entrepreneurs, and how to develop creative solutions to address social problems utilising Gandhi's model of 'be the change you wish to see in the world' to make a difference in the lives of others.

Name: The Fundamental Science of Nanotechnology
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: A ten-week course taken entirely online. It explains the mathematical foundations for nanoscale phenomena, as well as their effects and applications including quantum dots, nanotubes and fullerenes.

Name: The Impressionists: Painting Modern Life (Online)
About Course: Examine the major concerns of artists such as Cézanne, Monet, Manet and Degas and their intimate interaction with modern life.

Name: Writing Fiction (Online)
About Course: This course is for those who would like to write but don't know how; who tried once and gave up; or who already write but would like to improve; and for readers who have no desire to write but want a different perspective on how fiction works.

Name: Art Nouveau across Europe (Online)
About Course: From Paris to Moscow, Glasgow to Barcelona, this course examines the richness and variety of European art nouveau.

Name: Artificial Intelligence Concepts: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Aimed at a general audience, including professionals and those with no prior knowledge, this course provides an essential introduction to the key topics underpinning Artificial Intelligence.

Name: Artificial Intelligence Concepts: Introduction to Machine Learning (Online)
About Course: Machine Learning methods lie at the heart of the Artificial Intelligence revolution. This course introduces fundamental concepts to explain Machine Learning methods, potential, and pitfalls to a general audience.

Name: Critical Reasoning: A Romp through the Foothills of Logic (Online)
About Course: Reasoning enables us to acquire knowledge, to persuade others and to evaluate their arguments. But only if we reason well. We shall be learning how to recognise, evaluate, construct and analyse arguments, and how to recognise common fallacies.

Name: Exploring the Universe (Online)
About Course: How old is the universe? How unusual is the Solar System? How will it all end? Oxford astronomers Chris Lintott and Robert Simpson provide an overview of the last 13.7 billion years of cosmic evolution, answering these questions and more.

Name: Henry VIII (Online)
About Course: The reign of Henry VIII transformed British history. This course charts the political, religious and cultural changes of the period.

Name: Jane Austen (Online)
About Course: Many readers enjoy Austen's novels, but what makes them so special and enduring?

Name: Learning to Look at Modern Art (Online)
About Course: This course will seek to provide guidelines about how to look at modern art in an open-minded, critical and analytical way.

Name: Learning to Look at the Visual Arts (Online)
About Course: This course offers you the opportunity to learn how to study and analyse paintings, drawings and prints, and learn the 'language of looking'.

Name: Macroeconomics: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: This course provides a detailed introduction to, and encompasses the fundamentals of macroeconomics. On completion of the course you will have the ability to critically assess real-world macroeconomic developments at first-year undergraduate level.

Name: Political Philosophy: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Political philosophy contains some of the greatest writings in the Western intellectual tradition. This online course introduces you to the central questions concerning the state, by means of classical and contemporary texts.

Name: Ritual and Religion in Prehistory (Online)
About Course: How can we begin to understand the spiritual lives of prehistoric people? When do religious ideologies first appear on the human evolutionary timescale? Using both anthropology and archaeological evidence these and many other questions are examined.

Name: Theory of Knowledge (Online)
About Course: The theory of knowledge is one of the most central areas of philosophy. In this online course you will cover the key issues in epistemology while also learning to think for yourself and develop your own answers to the core questions in this area.

Name: Artificial Intelligence: Generative AI, Cloud and MLOps (online)
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: This online course covers workflows for designing and developing autonomous AI agents and systems using Cloud, non-Generative (classical) AI, Generative AI, and MLOps.

Name: Gene Technologies and Medicine
About Course: Fast-growing advances in gene technologies are shaping biomedical science. A long list of emerging technologies have been developed. Explore the basics about gene technologies and their applications in medicine discoveries.

Name: Illness in Victorian Literature
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Illness loomed large in the Victorian period, and in this day school leading scholars on the topic will introduce you to important ways in which it was a central preoccupation of Victorian literature.

Name: An Operatic Journey
About Course: A journey through operatic history, pausing at ten important turning points on the way, starting at the birth of opera in Italy around 1600 and ending in 'fin-de-siècle' Paris at the turn of the 20th century.

Name: Ancient Greek: Lower Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: The course focuses on analysing original passages from some of the greatest ancient Greek authors, tackling some challenging grammatical and syntactical phenomena and learning about ancient Greek culture and thought.

Name: Biblical Studies: The Bible, Its Content and Theology: An Introduction
About Course: Introduction to the content of the Old Testament/Hebrew Bible and the New Testament, together with their religious and socio-political backgrounds, languages and main theological themes and interpretations.

Name: Bioethics for Beginners (Online)
About Course: Do you think reproductive cloning is morally permissible? Do you check food labels to exclude buying any with GM ingredients? Would you worry if the government introduced compulsory depositing of DNA in the national DNA bank?

Name: Brontës (Online)
About Course: How did three sisters living apparently secluded, eventless lives write such original, passionate and dramatic literature?

Name: Bronze Age Europe: New Insights into Mobility and Cultural Contact
About Course: Current research on the human body is revealing insight into the mobility and cultural lifeways of ancient people. We focus on Bronze Age Europe and consider the range of archaeological evidence that offers new understandings on the fluidity of people.

Name: C++ Programming: Introduction
About Course: C++ will be used to introduce object-oriented programming, commencing at an introductory level. We will move onto encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, software engineering, dynamic data allocation, recursion as well as the standard template library.

Name: Calculus: Intermediate
About Course: The tools of calculus are used to understand the universe making it essential for all mathematical modelling. This course introduces the idea of multi-variable functions through partial differentiation and PDEs. Follows from OUDCE's 'Beginning Calculus'.

Name: Counselling: An Introduction
About Course: An introduction to the main schools of Counselling and Psychotherapy, as well as to basic counselling skills. Sessions will include presentations and discussions, and skills practice sessions in groups of 2 to 4 people. No previous experience is required.

Name: Daily Life in Byzantium
About Course: The course will offer an overview of the everyday life and culture of the Byzantine empire. Topics will include the social structure, commerce and industry, monasticism, family life, public welfare, the role of women, food and drink, education.

Name: Ethics: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: In this introduction to ethics, we shall examine four important ethical theories, applying them to two practical questions: the rights of animals and euthanasia. There will be plenty of opportunity to engage in debate and test your own thinking.

Name: French: Lower Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Explore the language and culture of French-speaking countries through this interactive class. A Lower Intermediate continuation course providing progression for students who completed French: Lower Intermediate - Part 1.

Name: Further Music Theory
About Course: This is a practical course for those interested in gaining knowledge and understanding of classical harmony. The course will cover the basics of harmony by taking the students through a series of straightforward, structured exercises.

Name: Islamic Art and Architecture (Online)
About Course: This course is for anyone interested in understanding Islamic art and culture, and examines the relationship between faith and art forms.

Name: Italian: Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Consolidate your proficiency in Italian language and express your opinions on topics which are familiar or of personal interest. A progression course for students who completed Italian: Intermediate - Part 1.

Name: Learn to Sing - I
About Course: For anyone with a passion for learning to sing. We will discuss and practise the fundamentals of vocal technique and interpretation, enabling you to produce a well-supported and stable vocal tone.

Name: Learning to Look at Western Architecture (Online)
About Course: This course is designed to enable you to 'read' the architecture of the Western world in a critically informed way.

Name: Literary Theory: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Although literary theory might sometimes seem intimidating, it can be very accessible and exciting. This course aims to demystify literary theory, showing how it illuminates literary texts and enriches our understanding and enjoyment of literature.

Name: Memoir: New Techniques, New Approaches
About Course: Every day we meet people with interesting life stories. Everyone is exotic to someone else. We shall look at contemporary memoirs that are tragic, uplifting, humorous and wise, and learn how to present the pattern of ourselves to others.

Name: Minoans and Mycenaeans (Online)
About Course: The Minoans and Mycenaeans left us with the intriguing Greek Bronze Age sites of Knossos, Mycenae, Pylos and Akrotiri. The excavation of these sites turned archaeologists into superstars, as stunning architecture, sculpture and weaponry were revealed.

Name: New Voices in Film: Charting the Growth of Marginalised Voices in Film
About Course: This course will uncover new voices in cinema, exploring how various minority and under-represented groups have fought to be represented fairly and accurately on screen.

Name: Person-Centred Approach to Therapy: An Introduction
About Course: Whether you are a counsellor already, keen to understand the power of this approach, wish to integrate it into your own practice, or a professional in one of the many disciplines that have been influenced by it, then this course should fascinate you.

Name: Philosophy of Science (Online)
About Course: This course introduces key issues in the philosophy of science, including debates about the nature of the scientific method, theories of confirmation, the demarcation of science from non-science, the rationality of theory change, and scientific realism.

Name: Screenwriting: From Pitch to Screen
About Course: This practical workshop builds on your awareness of writing techniques from the earlier module or other screenwriting courses, and enables you to write a feature-length screenplay or TV series, with guidance from a film industry tutor and peers.

Name: Shakespeare (Online)
About Course: This course focuses on five Shakespeare plays, covering a range of genres and periods of his writing.

Name: The Origins of the First World War
About Course: The First World War was a cataclysmic event. This course examines international relations before 1914, the countries which fought the war, how it started, the expectations of the participants, and assesses the war's historical significance,

Name: The Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence
About Course: Artificial intelligence is everywhere we look. But what do we mean by "intelligent"? Do machines "think"? Does AI have the potential of becoming self-aware or conscious? Do we need to fear the singularity? Can we align AI with our human values and ethics?

Name: The Reign of Edward I
About Course: Hailed by the English as a second Arthur, but reviled by his enemies as ‘the Covetous King’, Edward I was one of the most forceful kings in Britain’s history. What were the contemporary expectations of kingship which shaped his reign?

Name: Transpersonal Psychology: An Introduction
About Course: Dive into transpersonal psychology, exploring spiritual dimensions of human experience through theories, practices, and real-world applications. Engage with meditation, therapy techniques, and reflective learning for personal and professional growth.

Name: Tudors, Pagans and Goths:  A History of the Gothic Revival
About Course: British architecture is known for historical referencing, especially of the Gothic and Tudor periods.  This course examines the ideas and intentions of the architects, designers and builders behind this distinctively British approach to design.

Name: World Archaeology
About Course: In World Archaeology we explore the emergence of fascinating past societies from around the world. Some are mysterious and lost in the mists of time, while others form the foundations of cultural traditions that exist in the world today.

Name: Writing Fiction for Young Adults (Online)
About Course: Find your own voice and your own niche in writing for young adults, in sub-genres from realism to the supernatural.

Name: Writing Poetry (Online)
About Course: How can poetic form help you to turn the passion and intensity of life into memorable expressions? How can an appreciation of the techniques used by past and living poets help you to improve as a poet? Take this course and find out.

Name: Ancient India: From Indus Valley to Rise of Buddhism
About Course: This course introduces the archaeology of ancient South Asia. From the mighty Himalayas in the north to the waters of the Indian Ocean in the south, we will explore the archaeology and very early history of the region from 3000 to 500 BCE.

Name: Applied Data Science: Introduction
About Course: An intermediate course introducing a blend of data science concepts and technologies in order to enable you to work with everyday data related issues analytically. Gain experience of the entire data science supply chain with a hands-on group project.

Name: Augustine of Hippo: A Controversial Life
About Course: Augustine, the famous 5th-century North African bishop: profound philosopher, brilliant writer and preacher, fierce debater. Together we will read a wide selection of his works, including some transcripts of his sermons, to let him speak for himself.

Name: Believing the Unbelievable: Cults & Conspiracy Theories, Fake News & Feng Shui
About Course: What are the key warning signs that we are dealing with a seductive if ultimately irrational belief system?

Name: Botanical Connections: Plant Relationships with Other Life Forms
About Course: How does the stationary nature of plant life necessitate its connections with other living things? The course will explore plant behaviour as positive, negative, as well as neutral interactions with microbes, animals, plants, as well as humans.

Name: Changing Ireland: Fictional Perspectives
About Course: Irish fiction has acquired a high international profile since the 1990s, by reflecting the major transformations that reshaped the culture. This course examines four novels that illuminate the present by re-reading the past on both sides of the border.

Name: Chinese (Mandarin): Beginners - Part 2
About Course: Join this interactive course to further develop your basic Chinese (Mandarin) language skills and enjoy exploring the culture. For those who have completed Beginners - Part 1 and new students who have studied the language formally for one term.

Name: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT): An Introduction
About Course: An introduction to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy that will enable both experienced clinicians from other therapeutic traditions and people with a general interest in therapy to gain a foundation in key CBT theory and skills.

Name: Ethics with Aristotle
About Course: Why engage with an approach to ethics that is 2,300 years old? Because ethics without Aristotle is inconceivable, and his insights into what is good for humans remain invaluable. Join in to explore and discuss the 'Nicomachean Ethics'.

Name: Existential Therapy: An Introduction
About Course: This introduction to Existential Therapy will enable both experienced clinicians from other therapeutic traditions and those with a general interest in therapy to gain a foundation in key existential theory and skills.

Name: French: Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Consolidate your proficiency in French language and express your opinions on topics which are familiar or of personal interest. A progression course for students who completed French: Intermediate - Part 1.

Name: Getting Started in Nature Writing
About Course: Gain an appreciation of different forms of nature writing and produce your own texts in a supportive environment with this short online course.

Name: Japanese: Beginners - Part 2
About Course: Join this interactive course to further develop your basic Japanese language skills and enjoy exploring the culture. For those who have completed Beginners - Part 1 and new students who have studied the language formally for one term.

Name: Macaronis, Molls and the Mob: Society, Class and Gender in Georgian Satire
About Course: Why was Georgian England such a rich source of popular media, from the press to satirical caricature? What does that reveal about the changing nature of the Georgian world? We will explore these themes through the captivating eyes of contemporary print.

Name: Portuguese: Lower Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Explore the language and culture of Portuguese-speaking countries through this interactive class. A Lower Intermediate continuation course providing progression for students who completed Japanese: Lower Intermediate - Part 1.

Name: Poverty, Charity and Poor Relief in the Old Poor Law era 1550-1834
About Course: As population grew from 1550-1834, the proportion of people living in poverty increased. We explore the causes of poverty, the methods evolved to relieve or control the poor through charity and official poor relief, and the experience of being poor.

Name: Psychodynamic Counselling: An Introduction
About Course: An introduction to key psychodynamic concepts and practices including self-reflection applied to the understanding of human relationships. Based on psychoanalytical theory.

Name: Psychotherapeutic Counselling: An Introduction
About Course: Exploring human development and relationships from a therapeutic perspective. The ten week programme provides transferrable skills and a basic introduction to counselling for those who may wish to progress to further training.

Name: Python Programming for Data Science: Intermediate
About Course: Gain insight into advanced data science programming tools, using the Python programming language, to extract features from data, assess the statistical significance of the results found, and scale up the computational capability for big data challenges.

Name: Python Programming for Data Science: Intermediate
About Course: Gain insight into advanced data science programming tools, using the Python programming language, to extract features from data, assess the statistical significance of the results found, and scale up the computational capability for big data challenges.

Name: Python Programming for Data Science: Introduction
About Course: Gain insight into the most important programming tools using the Python programming language, for obtaining data, bringing it into a usable form, exploring and modelling it, and for presenting discoveries to a wider audience.

Name: Sacred Landscapes and Spiritual Journeys: Pilgrimage in the Western Tradition
About Course: What does pilgrimage mean to people today? What did it mean in the Middle Ages? Focusing on pilgrimage in western culture, this course explores how pilgrims’ beliefs, practices and experiences have continued, developed and changed over time.

Name: Soul Sisters: Women in Scripture and Early Christianity
About Course: Get to know a fascinating group of influential women who helped to shape the life and beliefs of early Christian communities. Together we will consider the status and identity of women in society, scripture and the first five centuries of the Church.

Name: Spanish: Lower Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Explore the language and culture of Spanish-speaking countries through this interactive class. A Lower Intermediate continuation course providing progression for students who completed Spanish: Lower Intermediate - Part 1.

Name: The Art and Archaeology of Geometric and Archaic Greece
About Course: Join us to explore, through rich learning materials and a museum visit, the art and archaeology of Geometric and Archaic Greece (ca. 1000-480 BCE), when the Greek alphabet, the Olympics and the Persian Wars changed the course of western identity.

Name: The Practice of Magic in Medieval Society
About Course: 'Magic' was a wide-ranging concept that affected many aspects of medieval society. This course will consider the actual and perceived practices of magic in the medieval period and their consequences.

Name: Women and the Arts of Byzantium
About Course: Reassess the role of women in the Byzantine world by studying case studies where visual arts, architecture, and material culture reveal female agency.

Name: A History of British Poetry from Shakespeare to Blake
About Course: Have you ever wanted to know more about poetry but didn't know where to start? If so, this lively and accessible course is for you. Together, we will close read a selection of poems in English from the mid 16th to the late 18th centuries.

Name: Ancestral Voices: The Earliest English Literature (Online)
About Course: This course introduces you to Old English literature: from tales of heroism, courage and fellowship, to poignant elegies of love and loss.

Name: Anthropology Applied
About Course: Explore the unique role of applied anthropology in addressing major global challenges of our time. Learn how an integrated understanding of social and cultural dynamics can make the difference between life and death, and change the way you view the world.

Name: Arabic: Beginners - Part 2
