About Course: Join this interactive course to further develop your basic Arabic language skills and enjoy exploring the culture. For those who have completed Beginners - Part 1 and new students who have studied the language formally for one term.

Name: Archaeology in Practice (Online)
About Course: How do archaeologists recognise and interpret the lives of past peoples and their societies? An introduction to the methods and techniques of archaeological enquiry, from initial site survey and excavation to scientific analysis.

Name: Art in Britain: Constable to Henry Moore
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: This lecture series will chart the broad history of painting and sculpture in Britain, from the Industrial Revolution to the 1930s: from the idyllic rural landscapes of Constable to the hard-edged Modernist abstractions of Hepworth and Moore.

Name: Artificial Intelligence Concepts: Practical Applications (Online)
About Course: Understanding the impact of Artificial Intelligence, now and in the future, is a key skill in the knowledge economy. This course develops a critical understanding of real-world AI applications by introducing various case studies to a general audience.

Name: Choral Masterpieces: From Bach to Britten
About Course: The rich combination of soloists, chorus and orchestra has inspired composers to produce some of their most profound works.  We will study ten of these masterpieces, from Bach to Britten, exploring the text, music and historical background.

Name: Constable and Turner: Aspects of Modernity
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: This lecture will explore the contrasting approaches to landscape painting taken by Constable and Turner. Were the gentle Suffolk landscapes of Constable as idyllic as they at first appear? And what drove Turner’s fascination with the immensity of nature?

Name: English Landscape Gardens: 1650 to the Present Day (Online)
About Course: This course is the ideal introduction to English garden history. It provides an overview of five centuries of development, from baroque formalism through the naturalistic landscape style, right up to contemporary cutting-edge planting style.

Name: Europe of the Dictators (Online)
About Course: Why were the inter-war years a period of such political extremism and dictatorial rule across Europe?

Name: Exploring the Basics of Human Nutrition
About Course: A person’s body requires the ingestion of food components to fulfil its basic functions. This is referred to as Nutrition. You will learn about the main food groups and the methods for determining if a Diet provides enough nutrients and promotes health.

Name: Film Analysis and Interpretation: A Beginner's Guide
About Course: A beginners course aimed at students with an interest in cinema but with little or no experience of film analysis or critical film theory. The course will introduce a range of concepts to develop skills and knowledge for the deep analysis of film texts.

Name: French: Beginners - Part 2
About Course: Join this interactive course to further develop your basic French language skills and enjoy exploring the culture. For those who have completed Beginners - Part 1 and new students who have studied the language formally for one term.

Name: Geology, Landscape and People
About Course: Geology determines the underlying nature of landscape, but mankind has utilised, modified and shaped the Earth's surface through several millennia of occupation. We examine the roles of geology and people in forming a range of distinctive landscapes.

Name: Getting Started Writing Your Feature Film Screenplay
About Course: Work actively to understand key screenwriting concepts to build your awareness of the needs of your film idea. Develop this into a riveting outline, populate it with engaging characters, and draw your audience into your story world though genre.

Name: Gothic to Renaissance : Architectural Transition in Italy
About Course: Italy's adoption of its distinctive Gothic styles was remarkable. We will go on to examine the equally dramatic transition in both church and secular building to Renaissance architecture in the major cities including Florence, Milan, Rome and Venice.

Name: Great Medieval Christian and Islamic Philosophers
About Course: Some medieval Christian and Islamic philosophers have been highly influential in the history of western thought. This course is an introduction to the thought of some of these philosophers: Anselm; Aquinas; Ockham; al Kindi; al Farabi; al Ghazali.

Name: Hegel's Political Philosophy
About Course: Apologist for the Prussian state? Proto-totalitarian? Or liberal? This course will cut through the misconceptions and present Hegel's political philosophy in its full complexity and subtlety, by means of a close reading of his Philosophy of Right (1821).

Name: Infectious Disease Modelling: Mathematical Techniques
About Course: Mathematics can be used to describe patterns around the spread of infectious diseases and predict future trends. Aimed at a general audience, this course will cover key mathematical concepts for building and analysing models of disease transmission.

Name: Investigating the Victorians (Online)
About Course: Britain led the world in the nineteenth century, but what were the consequences of industrialisation and empire on British society?

Name: Italian: Beginners - Part 2
About Course: Join this interactive course to further develop your basic Italian language skills and enjoy exploring the culture. For those who have completed our Beginners - Part 1 course and new students who have studied the language formally for one term.

Name: Italian: Lower Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Explore the language and culture of Italian-speaking countries through this interactive class. A Lower Intermediate continuation course providing progression for students who completed Italian: Lower Intermediate - Part 1.

Name: Justice and knowledge: Do the oppressed know something that others don’t?
About Course: Are some people ignored, silenced, or limited in their access to knowledge due to their identity? How might this occur? In this short course we consider how some people’s knowledge might be ignored and whose responsibility it is to do something about it.

Name: Modernist Poetry 1910-1945
About Course: This course guides you through  'modernism' in English language poetry. It revolutionised poetry and changed it fundamentally. Where did it come from, who were the principal figures, and what defines poetry as modernist? And what happened to it?

Name: New World Archaeology
About Course: The peoples of the Americas are descended from Siberian and Asian groups travelling into the New World between 40,000 and 15,000 years ago. Archaeology reveals a myriad of unique lifeways, settlements, and artifacts.

Name: Orientalist Art: An Introduction
About Course: Enter the world of Orientalist art to draw out the realities, contradictions, and political motivations behind this visually stunning style.

Name: Origins of Human Behaviour (Online)
About Course: What makes humans different from other primates? When did we become human? This course will chart the development of human behaviour.

Name: Political Change in Britain since the 1960s
About Course: An introduction to to key events, developments, and controversies in British political history from the advent of the Wilson-led governments in 1964  to the 2016 UK EU Referendum and its immediate aftermath

Name: Politics: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: In addition to tracing the evolution of the modern state and political ideas and ideologies, this course focuses on issues that confront people from all parts of the world on a day-to-day basis.

Name: Public Policy Economics (Online)
About Course: All of us are affected by government policies, and governments place particular emphasis on economic policies. This course will equip you to evaluate the economic arguments made about public policy choices.

Name: R Programming for Data Science: Introduction
About Course: Learn about R programming with this online course. At an introductory level, this course provides you with a solid foundation of the R programming language. Here you will learn the basics of R and gradually move to data processing and manipulation.

Name: Spanish: Beginners - Part 2
About Course: Join this interactive course to further develop your basic Spanish language skills and enjoy exploring the culture. For those who have completed Beginners - Part 1 and new students who have studied the language formally for one term.

Name: Spanish: Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Consolidate your proficiency in Spanish language and express your opinions on topics which are familiar or of personal interest. A progression course for students who completed Spanish: Intermediate - Part 1.

Name: The Architecture of the English Medieval Cathedral (Online)
About Course: This course will explore the English medieval cathedral as a developing institution which survived over a thousand years of religious upheaval and historical change, focusing on the multifaceted architecture of a range of truly great churches.

Name: The Building Culture of Britain: From Vernacular to Sustainable Architecture
About Course: What links the ground beneath our feet to our cultural heritage? How do local building variations emerge and develop? Why is traditional building practice still important? Join this course to explore the material culture of historic buildings in Britain.

Name: The First Civilization: Mesopotamia (Online)
About Course: Civilization was born over 5,000 years ago on the fertile plains of southern Mesopotamia.  Using archaeology and textual sources, this course will build a picture of the Sumerian civilization, one that lies at the root of our own world.

Name: The History of Economic Thought (Online)
About Course: This course evaluates the development of economic thought through the eyes of Greek, Chinese, Indian and European traditions before exploring economic thought in the context of the 20th century.

Name: The Making of Modern Britain (Online)
About Course: A modern, democratic, multicultural Britain developed throughout the twentieth century. This course will examine the key social, economic and political influences that have shaped modern Britain.

Name: The Pianists' Workshop - II
About Course: Explore piano repertoire, interpretation and technique in a lively mixture of talks and workshops, in which all students will have regular opportunities to play. This class is open to players of all levels and students may join the class in any term.

Name: The Rise of British Overseas Trade in the 18th Century
About Course: This course examines how the growth of overseas trade helped Britain to dramatically redefine its place in the world in the long eighteenth century.

Name: Virginia Woolf on Writing Novels
About Course: This course will take you to Virginia Woolf's writing desk to look at the challenges of writing a novel from her perspective. Guided by her theory of fiction, we will gain insight into her unique voice in Jacob's Room, Mrs Dalloway and To the Lighthouse.

Name: Writing Drama (Online)
About Course: A creative and critical course helping you develop your passion for drama into the craft of dramatic writing.

Name: A History of Folklore
About Course: This course provides an historical introduction to the development of folklore studies in Britain. It will review historical conceptions and approaches to folklore from the seventeenth-century antiquarians to the present.

Name: A Troubled Britain: Two Centuries of Protest since 1815
About Course: From political agitation and religious discord to single-issue demands, British society has often  been confronted by dissenting voices. Starting in 1815 we will examine these protests, seeking to understand the nature of challenges to the status quo.

Name: Analytic Philosophy: Ten Classic Papers
About Course: We drill down into some of the classic papers of analytic philosophy, unpacking and analysing their arguments.

Name: Democracy and Bureaucracy: from the past to the future
About Course: The people who live in democracies that are based on universal equality often feel that they are actually governed by an unelected and hierarchical bureaucracy. We will study the pluses and minuses of these rival modern models of operation and control.

Name: Developing Your Novel and Polishing Your Work
About Course: A course for writers who feel stuck and need support to progress with, or finish, their novel.

Name: Environmental Ethics: Technology, Climate Justice and the Environment
About Course: Climate change is a major concern of today. It raises many ethical questions about what we should do, what obligations we have to others and how we should relate to the natural world. This course will examine some of those questions.

Name: Florence, Rome and Venice: The Architecture of the Italian Renaissance
About Course: Join us to explore the rich and dazzling architecture of the Italian Renaissance in three key cities. We will investigate the differing ways in which the classical styles of the Renaissance found expression in Florence, Rome and Venice.

Name: German: Beginners - Part 2
About Course: Join this interactive course to further develop your basic German language skills and enjoy exploring the culture. For those who have completed Beginners - Part 1 and new students who have studied the language formally for one term.

Name: German: Lower Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Explore the language and culture of German-speaking countries through this interactive class. A Lower Intermediate continuation course providing progression for students who completed German: Lower Intermediate - Part 1.

Name: Great Love Stories
About Course: People have always experienced love but literary depictions have changed dramatically. This course will explore classic love stories from Shakespeare to the present. Authors include Jane Austen, Thomas Hardy and Gabriel García Márquez.

Name: Henry James: Early, Middle, Late
About Course: A study of three novels from the early, middle and late stages of Henry James's career, Roderick Hudson, The Portrait of a Lady and The Wings of the Dove.  Each explores James's favourite subjects: the international theme, vicarious living, human choice.

Name: Japanese: Lower Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Explore the language and culture of Japanese-speaking countries through this interactive class. A Lower Intermediate continuation course providing progression for students who completed Japanese: Lower Intermediate - Part 1.

Name: Korean: Beginners - Part 2
About Course: Join this interactive course to further develop your basic Korean language skills and enjoy exploring the culture. For those who have completed Beginners - Part 1 and new students who have studied the language formally for one term.

Name: Latin: Beginners - Part 2
About Course: This course continues to introduce the basic principles of Classical Latin. It provides a firm basis of grammar, sentence structure and vocabulary of the language, through which you will be able to read and translate Roman drama in adaptation.

Name: Latin: Lower Intermediate - Part 2
About Course: Continue developing your knowledge of Latin with this 10-week course. Besides learning some new grammar and fundamental syntax, you will read some texts adapted from Cicero, about the corruption of the governor Verres.

Name: Linear Algebra: Intermediate
About Course: Linear Algebra is fundamental to Geometry, Statistics, Analysis and most topics in Mathematics. From solving linear equations to abstraction, this course develops deeper knowledge with rigorous proofs. This follows on from Linear Algebra: Introduction.

Name: Magic and Heresy in Medieval Europe
About Course: In this course students will develop an understanding of magic and heresy in High and Late Medieval Europe, and the ways in which these played a role in the appearance of witchcraft towards the end of the Middle Ages.

Name: Materiality and Meaning: Exploring Prehistoric Britain Through Material Culture
About Course: Materiality in archaeology is an approach to investigation that focuses on relationships between people and the materials and places they create, modify, and interact with. How can archaeologists best understand British prehistory through materiality?

Name: Mindfulness and Meditation: The Art and Science of Self-transformation
About Course: Explore the theory and practice of mindfulness/meditation effects within Eastern and Western religious traditions and in a modern therapeutic context. Try out various techniques. Learn about the art and science of meditation, including its controversies.

Name: Portuguese: Beginners - Part 2
About Course: Join this interactive course to further develop your basic Portuguese language skills and enjoy exploring the culture. For those who have completed our Beginners - Part 1 course and new students who have studied the language formally for one term.

Name: Reading Literature Critically
About Course: With an emphasis on close critical analysis, this course is designed to enable you to become a more attentive, appreciative and critical reader of literary texts.

Name: Songwriting: An Introduction
About Course: This practical course will teach the skills common to all types/styles of songwriting. No previous composing experience is necessary for full participation, just basic musical literacy and an interest in learning to write songs.

Name: The Beethoven Piano Sonatas
About Course: The piano was, for Beethoven, his most personal means of expression and his monumental cycle of piano sonatas is one of the pinnacles of western music. This course will explore these works chronologically.

Name: The River Thames from Mouth to Source - An Architectural Journey
About Course: Join us to take an imaginary journey up the Thames, from the mouth between Essex and Kent, to its sources amid the rolling countryside of Wiltshire and Gloucestershire.

Name: Women of Ancient Egypt: An Exploration of Non-Elite Female lives
About Course: Become acquainted with the domestic and working lives of Ancient Egypt's non-elite women. A life course journey from the perils of childbirth to the esteemed position of older wise women.

Name: A Pianist Explores
Mode: In-person day/weekend- Short courses- Lecture series
About Course: A musical journey through the piano repertoire. In each lecture Jonathan Darnborough turns the spotlight on a single iconic piano work, with illustrations from the piano followed by a performance of the piece.

Name: Ancient Greek: Beginners - Part 2
About Course: This course builds on Part 1, and allows you to extend and revise your grammatical knowledge so far while reading some engaging texts in Greek.

Name: Animal Ethics: The Moral and Legal Status of Animals
About Course: Our thinking about non-human animals is, at best, confused. The purpose of this course will be to examine that confusion and to learn to think critically about the moral and legal status of non-human animals. No background in law/philosophy required.

Name: Feminist Philosophy
About Course: Feminism is a political movement aiming to end the oppression of women. But what is to be a 'woman'? Do women have distinctive ways of knowing and acting? What is gender injustice? The course engages with such core issues of feminist thought.

Name: Introduction to the Energy Transition
About Course: Introduction to the Energy Transition is a course that covers an increasingly important issue with respect to climate change, ecology, energy policies, supply disruption, and competition for energy.

Name: Mozart: Sonata in C, K 545, 1st movement
Mode: In-person day/weekend- Short courses- Lecture series
About Course: In this late work Mozart shows himself at his subtlest, achieving that Holy Grail for all creative artists, beauty with simplicity. This lecture is part of the 'A Pianist Explores' lecture series - providing a musical journey through the piano repertoire.

Name: Statistics for Data Science: Introduction
About Course: This course will introduce statistics to the beginner, covering measures of central tendency, dispersion, probability theory and inferential statistics.

Name: Sutton Hoo
About Course: This course will look at the Anglo-Saxon burial of Sutton Hoo, its excavation and finds, and the settlement, art and literature of the period. We will have an all-day coach trip to Sutton Hoo and West Stow village.

Name: Understanding Space and Time
About Course: A non-mathematical overview of the current scientific understanding of space and time. Including an introduction to Einstein's theory of relativity, its consequences, and applications.

Name: Women Artists of Scandinavia
About Course: Explore how Scandinavia and Finland produced some of the most talented artists in Europe in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

Name: Creating Successful Community History Projects: A Workshop
About Course: This day school will give those seeking to set up their own community or local history projects the opportunity to be inspired by and learn from those who have successfully run community or oral history projects in their own localities.

Name: Writing Historical Fiction
About Course: An action-packed day school in Oxford on how to write compelling historical fiction with award-winning historical novelist Rebecca Abrams. Come prepared to write, experiment and discover, and expect to leave enthused, informed and inspired.

Name: Civil War and Revolution: Britain Divided, 1640-1660 (Online)
About Course: The civil wars that swept across the British Isles in the 17th century left few lives untouched. This course will explore the causes, conduct and significance of the English civil wars.

Name: Drug Development, Pharmacokinetics and Imaging
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: This five-day short course from the Experimental and Translational Therapeutics Programme is taught through face-to-face tutorials. It discusses the basic principles of designing and identifying new drug molecules and monitoring their effect.

Name: Elizabeth I (Online)
About Course: This course will examine the life and reign of Elizabeth I, from her troubled childhood to the death of the aged Virgin Queen. But what do we really know of this iconic queen? Can her reign be accounted a success?

Name: Introduction to Statistics for Health Care Research
About Course: A flexible online statistics course for busy health and social care professionals who need to understand the basics of health statistics without becoming statisticians.

Name: Italian Renaissance Art c.1400-c.1600 (Online)
About Course: From Bellini and Botticelli to tapestry and tableware, the material culture of the Italian Renaissance continues to fascinate us to this day. This course is an opportunity to explore this unique period.

Name: Reality, Being and Existence: An Introduction to Metaphysics (Online)
About Course: An introduction to metaphysics, the most general investigation of reality. It has been at the centre of philosophy since the beginning of the Western tradition in ancient Greece, and many of its concerns are the same as those of Plato and Aristotle.

Name: Social Anthropology: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Social anthropology is the study of how humans give meaning to the world through different social norms, values, practices and means of organisation. This course provides an exciting and dynamic introduction to the world of social anthropology.

Name: Social Policy and Welfare States in the 21st Century (Online)
About Course: What is the welfare state and what functions does it serve? Why and how do welfare states vary across countries and over time? What are the biggest challenges that welfare states face in the 21st century?

Name: The Culture of the English Country House (Online)
About Course: Explore the culture of the English country house from its architectural form, social manners and distinctions to the furnishings and artistic manifestations of taste, as an expression of power and influence in a changing society.

Name: The First World War in Perspective (Online)
About Course: This course seeks to explain why and how the First World War was fought, and to understand why its legacy remains relevant more than a century after it ended.

Name: The Modern American Novel: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: In this course we shall study five key novels of the twentieth century - by Fitzgerald, Faulkner, Silko, Morrison and Roth.

Name: The Number Mysteries (Online)
About Course: It is hard to imagine a world without numbers, but how natural is mathematics? We explore this very question through numerous online activities and 'at home' experiments, which allow you to interact with mathematics as you will never have done before.

Name: Vikings: Raiders, Traders and Settlers (Online)
About Course: Ravagers, despoilers, pagans, the Vikings are often regarded as bloodthirsty pirates. Yet they were also traders, settlers and farmers with a thriving artistic culture and legal systems.  Using archaeology we examine the varied aspects of the Viking world

Name: Humanism: An Introduction
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: An investigation into humanism in its contemporary sense (sometimes called ‘secular humanism’). What is the humanist alternative to religious world-views, and what are its strengths and weaknesses? Join us for this series of lectures in Oxford or online.

Name: Academic Art and the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Investigate the complex relationship between the established academic arts of the mid-19th century, and the innovations of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood. Artists whose work will feature include Millais, Rossetti and Hunt. Join in Oxford or watch online.

Name: Material Legacies of Empire
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: This three-day course will offer Continuing Professional Development to heritage sector professionals. It will focus on the material legacy of Empire and colonialism through paintings, decorative arts and the built environment.

Name: Exploring Cognition
About Course: We will take a brief look at the workings of the brain, and how psychologists describe the functions of attention, perception and memory. Explore how these processes can work to fool us, and what we have learned from dysfunction.

Name: Beethoven: 'Moonlight' Sonata, Op. 27, no. 2, 1st movement
Mode: In-person day/weekend- Short courses- Lecture series
About Course: The poet Rellstab compared the first movement of this iconic work with the play of moonlight on the waters of a lake. Concealed beneath the dreamy surface of this movement, however, is a structure every bit as tight as anything Beethoven ever wrote.

Name: Climate Change in Science Fiction: Film, Literature and Gaming
About Course: Climate change has been a feature of Science Fiction narratives for longer than it has been recognised as a scientific reality. This day school takes a look at climate fiction across science fiction film, literature, graphic novels and gaming.

Name: Contemporary Developments in Coaching
About Course: Drawing on psychology, sociology, anthropology and education, this day aims to help coaches of all backgrounds and levels of experience explore recent developments that affect their practice, highlight sources and pinpoint themes to watch in the future.

Name: Maximising Productivity: LLMs and ChatGPT for Coders
About Course: This hands-on day focuses on how to utilise the power of LLMs for tasks including, but not limited to, Automated Code Generation, Completion and Optimisation, Documentation Writing, Test Case Formulation and Code Translation Across Languages.

Name: Unwrapping the Galloway Hoard
About Course: Buried in Viking Age Britain around 900 CE, the Galloway Hoard is a rich collection of rare and unique objects. This event brings together a team of archaeologists and conservators working on the hoard to explore both its contents and meaning.

Name: Developing Practice in Medical Education
About Course: Using critical reflection as a framework to relate theoretical and conceptual models to practice, taking into account evidence, values, learner diversity and modes of learning.

Name: Mixing it up: understanding and using mixed methods research in social sciences
About Course: An online course for researchers which critically discusses mixed methods approaches to social science analysis.

Name: Intimations of Modernism: Ruskin and Whistler
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Should painters depict moral subjects in sharp-edged clarity? Or should painting echo the abstractions of music in its depictions of the modern industrial world? This lecture will address these questions, with reference to the Ruskin-Whistler controversy.

Name: Mendelssohn: Variations Sérieuses, Op. 54
Mode: In-person day/weekend- Short courses- Lecture series
About Course: Reacting against the empty display of variations by the virtuosi of his day, Mendelssohn wrote his Variations Sérieuses as a homage to Beethoven. Basing them on a poignant theme, Mendelssohn explores a wide range of moods, ending in a jubilant finale.

Name: Thinking Machines and the Ethics of AI
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Robots, cyborgs and AI systems fire our imaginations and have inspired many movies, from HAL in '2001: A Space Odyssey' to Data in 'Star Trek' and Skynet in 'The Terminator'. What moral issues do they raise?

Name: W.B. Yeats and His Poetry, 1920-30s
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: W.B. Yeats was one of the most influential and important poets of the twentieth century. During his long career, his poetry had many forms. This day school looks at his work during the 1920s and 30s. Join us in Oxford or online.

Name: Ethics and Justice in Translational Science
About Course: Conceptual and theoretical approaches to ethical issues in translational health sciences

Name: Evidence-Based Diagnosis and Screening
About Course: Critical appraisal and application, at an advanced level, of the best evidence on diagnostic tests.

Name: Bird Biodiversity and Population Monitoring Methods
About Course: Part-time over five weeks, this tutor-led training course can be taken from anywhere in the world. It will appeal to students and practitioners who want to improve their ability to conduct bird surveys.

Name: Data Analysis in Ecology: Statistics for Ecologists & Field Biologists (10-week)
About Course: A 10-week, tutor-led data analysis course taken entirely online. The course introduces students to the use of QED Statistics and R software.

Name: Intimations of the Avant-Garde: Camden Town and the London Group
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Consider the earliest full manifestations of European Modernism in British art. Walter Sickert, Harold Gilman, Roger Fry, Mark Gertler and Stanislawa de Karlowska will be discussed. Part of the 'Art in Britain: Constable to Henry Moore' lecture series.

Name: Chopin: Nocturne in D-flat, Op. 27, no. 2
Mode: In-person day/weekend- Short courses- Lecture series
About Course: In this famous Nocturne, Chopin combines the dreamy with the dramatic in an apparently improvisatory stream of consciousness that belies the time he devoted to its composition. This lecture is part of the 'A Pianist Explores' lecture series.

Name: Building Assignment Writing Skills
About Course: Whether you are new to study or have a problem with some aspect of essay-writing, this workshop will help you to develop a systematic approach to planning, writing and presenting your assignment.

Name: The Art of the Home in the Renaissance and Early Modern World
About Course: Explore the art of the home in the Renaissance and early modern world, from colourful ceramics and incense burners to paintings and tapestries in interiors across the Mediterranean and Eurasia.

Name: Vorticism and Total War
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: This lecture will focus on the hard-edged Modernism of the Vorticist group, and the various ways in which British artists responded to the advent of Cubism and the First World War. Featured artists include Wyndham Lewis, Jacob Epstein and C.R.W Nevinson.

Name: Rachmaninoff: Prelude in D, Op. 23, no. 4
Mode: In-person day/weekend- Short courses- Lecture series
About Course: In his D major Prelude, Rachmaninoff weaves one of his characteristic extended melodies and builds towards a climax of shattering intensity. This lecture is part of the 'A Pianist Explores' lecture series.

Name: Impressionism in Art and Music
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: An exploration of the artistic movement that came to embrace both art and music, looking at the major visual and musical works of the Impressionists, and tracing the roots of this aesthetic upheaval that laid the foundations for modernism in the arts.

Name: Intersectionality and Globalisation
About Course: We will explore how sex, gender and inequality interact within globalized economies, with an emphasis on an intersectional perspective, while navigating through the complexities of evolving labour markets, climate change and technological challenges.

Name: Realist Reviews and Realist Evaluation
About Course: Aiming to provide an understanding of realist reviews and evaluation and the ability to apply new knowledge and skills to a realist research project.

Name: Unit One and British Modernism
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Lecture series- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Explore British art during the interwar period. How did British artists react to the arrival of Surrealism in Britain? Featured artists include Barbara Hepworth, Paul Nash and Henry Moore. Part of the 'Art in Britain' lecture series.

Name: Queens of Egypt: An Exploration of Elite Female Power
About Course: To what extent could an elite females exercise power in ancient Egypt? How were some women able to rise through a male dominated hierarachy to rule Egypt? This course examines exceptional female rulers including Hatshepsut and Cleopatra VII.

Name: Scriabin: Sonata no. 5, Op. 53
Mode: In-person day/weekend- Short courses- Lecture series
About Course: Described by Horowitz as the most difficult piano piece ever written, legend has it that this sonata came to Scriabin in a dream. This lecture is part of the 'A Pianist Explores' lecture series - providing a musical journey through the piano repertoire.

Name: Machine Learning with R
About Course: Gain the practical skills needed in using R for machine learning tasks. Covering many concepts and hands-on applications, the day delves into various machine learning algorithms, data preprocessing techniques and model evaluation methods.

Name: Problem Solving and Critical Thinking
About Course: Gain the knowledge and understanding of Problem Solving and Critical Thinking at this day event in Oxford. Interactive sessions will explain skills and use tools to help you improve your ability to work in these areas.

Name: The 1925 Paris Exposition des Arts Décoratifs and its Legacy
About Course: 2025 marks the centenary of the chicest international exposition of the 20th century. One of the defining events of Jazz Age visual culture, the event brought together some of the most exciting designers in Europe and gave its name to the Art Deco style.

Name: Patients, Citizens and the Politics of Evidence
About Course: Examining the role of patients and citizens in providing evidence for health care research

Name: Early Technological Behaviour: The Oldowan and Early Acheulian in Africa
About Course: Significant technological developments took place in Africa between 2 and 1.5 million years ago, including the emergence of new tools such as handaxes. This day school explores the stone and other technologies of this key period of the African stone age.

Name: Hip-Hop: A Cultural History
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: From its origins in 70s New York, hip-hop has become a global phenomenon. This day school charts the history of that development, looking also at the appearance of regional styles in the West Coast, southern states and abroad.

Name: Economics of Health Care
About Course: Using economics to improve health and healthcare

Name: Health Care Innovation and Technology
About Course: This five-day course provides a comprehensive overview of the use, potential benefits and dangers of technology in modern surgery.

Name: Pharmacodynamics, Biomarkers and Personalised Therapy
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: The pharmacodynamic process of drug therapy provides the link between the pharmacokinetic profile and the therapeutic effect of a drug. This course offers an introduction to pharmacodynamics and the principles of pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modelling.

Name: Ancient Mariners: The Global Archaeology of Seafaring and Exploration
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Chart the deep human history of seafaring across Earth’s oceans - from Ancient Egypt to Bronze Age Greece, Neolithic England to the Vikings, and Ice Age Australia to remote Pacific atolls. Join in Oxford or watch online.

Name: The Psychology of Addiction
About Course: Addiction is a complex construct in which an individual takes a substance or engages in behaviour that is pleasurable but eventually becomes compulsive with harmful consequences. This day offers interesting multidimensional explanations of addiction.

Name: Writing Fiction Essentials: Character, Description and Dialogue
About Course: An inspiring and informative weekend event exploring the essentials of writing prose fiction with award-winning writer Rebecca Abrams.

Name: Ethics of the Beginning and End of Life
About Course: An introduction to basic questions and concepts in reproductive ethics and end of life decisions, as well as more general philosophical questions about the value of life and badness of death.

Name: Fish and Amphibian Survey Methods
About Course: Part-time over five weeks, this tutor-led training course can be taken from anywhere in the world. It will appeal to students and practitioners who want to improve their ability to conduct fish and amphibian surveys.

Name: Developing Further Assignment Writing Skills
About Course: A more advanced workshop for experienced essay and report writers who would like to improve the style and structure of their writing and to develop the technique of persuasive argument.

Name: Impact of Natural Products in Medicine
About Course: Medicinal products are developed from nature and may offer therapeutic benefit. This day school is designed to provide an understanding and insight into how medicinal products are discovered and developed into approved pharmaceutical agents for human use.

Name: Naseby: The Memory of a Battle in a Changing Landscape
About Course: This event will explore the Battle of Naseby, a turning point in British history. We will explore the battlefield itself (accessing locations not open to the public), why it occurred where it did, and how its participants determined Naseby’s outcome.

Name: Social Innovation and Entrepreneurship: Emerging Technologies
About Course: Learn how emerging technologies, such as AI and extended realities (VR/AR/MR), can empower social innovation, guiding you to develop tech-enhanced solutions for sustainable social change.

Name: Meta-analysis
About Course: Basic and advanced statistical methods for meta-analysis.

Name: Nanomedicine - Science and Applications
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: This five-day course provides a thorough overview of the exciting and emerging discipline of nanomedicine, which is already starting to transform the way that medical and health care solutions are developed and delivered.

Name: Election Forecasting
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Introducing a wide variety of different election forecasting methods for UK general elections. As well as pre-election forecasts, the day will cover exit poll methodology and seat prediction from early constituency results.

Name: The Films of Orson Welles
About Course: Acclaimed as a wunderkind of theatre and radio, Welles was seemingly destined to dominate 1940s Hollywood. By analysing key movies such as Citizen Kane, The Magnificent Ambersons and The Lady of Shanghai, we will chart his fascinating fall from grace.

Name: The Spectacular Universe: Astronomy Weekend
About Course: A celebration of the latest advances in astronomy, with some of the best images from satellites, space probes and ground-based observatories. With world-leading experts, all are welcome at this popular and richly illustrated event.

Name: Advanced Qualitative Research Methods
About Course: Advancing skills and knowledge of complex issues in qualitative research

Name: The Setting of Heritage Assets
Mode: In-person day/weekend- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: Increase your understanding of setting as it applies to heritage assets, along with its contribution to good design and the positive management of heritage assets. Aimed at UK-based historic environment practitioners and others in related disciplines.

Name: Context Matters: The Way Language is Used in Communication
About Course: An introduction to discourse analysis, the field of linguistics concerned with the study of language in context. We will look at what makes a stretch of language a piece of discourse and the varied uses of language in context.

Name: Extinctions: Crises in the History of Life
About Course: A wide-ranging introduction to extinction from a geological viewpoint. Topics include recent extinctions, mass extinctions and their likely causes, the role of extinction in evolution, plus a chance to study many real fossils in the teaching room.

Name: Thinking Critically about News Media
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: To what extent can we trust news provision? Where does news media end, and propaganda and manipulation begin? Join us in Oxford or online to learn more.

Name: Extinctions: Crises in the History of Life
About Course: A wide-ranging introduction to extinction from a geological viewpoint. Topics include recent extinctions, mass extinctions and their likely causes, the role of extinction in evolution, plus a chance to study many real fossils in the teaching room.

Name: Climate Change: Creative and Hopeful Responses
About Course: Join us for a dynamic half-day event with artists and researchers exploring climate change, creativity and hope. Afterwards, you are encouraged to go on a self-guided tour of the ‘Museum of Climate Hope’ trail across Oxford.

Name: Southern African Literary and Visual Cultures
About Course: Gain an appreciation and understanding of the exciting contemporary literary and visual cultures of the geographically, culturally and linguistically diverse region of Southern Africa. Many different forms of cultural production will be discussed.

Name: Oxford Advanced Pre-sessional Course for Graduate Students
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: The Oxford Advanced Pre-sessional Course is a challenging and intensive 9-week programme aimed at preparing students (both native and non-native speakers of English) for postgraduate degree programmes in the UK.

Name: A ‘Herstory’ of Art: Discovering Women Artists
About Course: This course examines the social, economic, religious, and political contexts under which women have always made art, but have largely been marginalised in its formal histories and markets.

Name: Applied Data Science: Introduction
About Course: An intermediate course introducing a blend of data science concepts and technologies in order to enable you to work with everyday data related issues analytically. Gain experience of the entire data science supply chain with a hands-on group project.

Name: Before Canterbury: Chaucer's Dream Visions and 'Troilus and Criseyde'
About Course: Best known for The Canterbury Tales, Chaucer's earlier work takes us to the fantastical worlds of dream vision and philosophical romance. We’ll explore 'The Book of the Duchess', 'The House of Fame', 'The Parliament of Fowls' and 'Troilus and Criseyde'.

Name: Chinese (Mandarin): Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This Chinese consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Climate Change and the Arts around the Mediterranean
About Course: The course will examine a broad selection of artistic case studies to understand how societies, visual arts, culture, and artists have responded to climate changes in the context of the Mediterranean basin, from Antiquity to the present.

Name: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT): An Introduction
About Course: An introduction to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy that will enable both experienced clinicians from other therapeutic traditions and people with a general interest in therapy to gain a foundation in key CBT theory and skills.

Name: Daily life in the Classical World
About Course: This course will explore the lived experiences of individuals in the urban Classical World, from the food they ate and the houses they lived in, to their beliefs, identities and well-being.

Name: Existential Therapy: An Introduction
About Course: This introduction to Existential Therapy will enable both experienced clinicians from other therapeutic traditions and those with a general interest in therapy to gain a foundation in key existential theory and skills.

Name: Existentialism and Ethics
About Course: An introduction into existentialist approaches to ethics and the ethical. With a particular focus on subjectivity and individual responsibility, we will ask what morality is and could be.

Name: Flash Fiction Workshop
About Course: Writing flash fiction brings benefits to writers of all stripes. In this hands-on workshop, we'll be writing each week, discussing our work, and developing new skills in brevity, language and form.

Name: French: Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This French consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: From Revolution to War: Europe, 1789-1914
About Course: This course examines the story of Europe in the nineteenth century focusing on the themes of national identity, political and economic development, colonial expansion and urban development. What was the historical legacy of these dramatic European events?

Name: Hollywood Masters: Otto Preminger
About Course: This course introduces the work of the major Hollywood director Otto Preminger, offering critical approaches to understanding his film style across a range of genres and his place within debates about film authorship

Name: Integral Human Development
About Course: There are developed and less developed economies, cultures, communities, and individuals. Can we integrate all these sorts of development into one desirable whole? This class will look at efforts to think holistically about the modern human condition.

Name: Japanese: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This Japanese consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Personalised Medicine: An Introduction
About Course: Our genes control our biological processes, and scientists are decoding their role in disease development to identify new clues for novel therapies. Gene technologies offer a new Personalized Medicine approach of treating patients as individuals.

Name: Political Economy of Human Behaviour and Economic Development
About Course: Economists assume that when we make choices we do so without our decisions being affected by anger, hate, hunger, fear, envy or just jealously. But to what extent is this true?

Name: Portuguese: Lower Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This Italian consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Python Programming for Data Science: Intermediate
About Course: Gain insight into advanced data science programming tools, using the Python programming language, to extract features from data, assess the statistical significance of the results found, and scale up the computational capability for big data challenges.

Name: Signals of Life: Concepts of Cellular Communication
About Course: The course will explore the inner workings of cells in organisms that enable them to sense and respond to their environment. Signalling systems that allow communication of an external signal to evoke a cellular response will be examined.

Name: Spanish: Lower Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This Spanish consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Systemic and Family Therapy: An Introduction
About Course: Focus on ways of observing and understanding the interactions between families, couples, organisations and professional relationships, with approaches that help people with psychological difficulties to mobilise the strengths of their relationships.

Name: The First English Novels
About Course: The novel emerged as a vital new literary genre during the long eighteenth century (c. 1688-1815). This course explores some of the earliest major novels written in English and provides an accessible introduction to their formal and thematic qualities.

Name: The First Person Perspective: From Phenomenal Consciousness to Intersubjectivity
About Course: Who or what can develop a first-person perspective? Our sense of self is an integral and fundamental part of conscious life, even in light of the fact that the maturation of the self appears to involve complex social processes.

Name: The Origins of Christian Mysticism
About Course: Come and discover the origins of Christian mystical theology.  Explore 'the seeing that consists in not seeing' (Gregory of Nyssa), the state of mind 'resembling sapphire' (Evagrius of Pontus), and 'the brilliant darkness of a hidden silence' (Dionysius).

Name: Understanding the Biodiversity Crisis: Introduction to Ecology and Conservation
About Course: Biodiversity loss is evident no matter where we live. To reverse the current decline, we need to understand how individual species interact with their environment, while also appreciating the practical strategies to monitor and conserve species.

Name: Web Applications using JavaScript: Introduction
About Course: An introduction to the essentials of web applications: HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Furthermore PHP, MySQL, React, Python's Django which introduce full-stack and cross-platform web application development.

Name: Advanced Creative Writing (Online)
About Course: A practical course covering all aspects of novel writing from character creation and story development to final edit.

Name: Advanced Writing Lives (Online)
About Course: Every day we meet people with interesting life stories.  Our lives are made up of tragic, uplifting and humorous experiences which shape us as individuals.  We love, fight, apologise, account for and endure through whatever comes our way.

Name: Adventures in Medieval Art
About Course: Medieval art glitters and enthrals. Medieval architecture elicits wonder and awe. In this introductory course you will learn about its breadth and diversity, from great cathedrals and imposing castles to sacred icons and subversive marginalia.

Name: Animal Behaviour: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Why do animals behave the way they do? In this course we will look at the full range of behaviours found in the animal kingdom, from simple escape behaviours to complex tool use and their evolution.

Name: Arabic: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This Arabic consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Climate change: Past, present and future
About Course: Climate affects the planning of our daily activities. Its variability also inflicts damage on individuals and entire economies and societies. We will explore how climate varies, in the past, present and future, and how this impacts on society.

Name: Critical Reading (Online)
About Course: This course is for anyone who would like to learn to read beneath the surface, pay attention to language and form, and become a critical reader.

Name: Ethics of Conflict: From Protest and Revolution to Terrorism and War
About Course: We explore conflict within the state (cancel culture, civil disobedience, terrorism, revolution) & between states (when to wage war; how to conduct ourselves during war & after victory; the future of war given AI, drones, cyberwarfare; cold war strategy).

Name: French: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This French consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Genomics Applications in Healthcare: An Introduction
About Course: Genome sequencing (Genomics) offer new opportunities for potential applications in healthcare and perhaps suggesting new therapies for diseases that were not treatable before.

Name: Getting Started in Creative Writing (Online)
About Course: This course introduces the key characteristics of creative writing. You will be supported with stage-by-stage guidance as you assimilate and employ a range of critical and creative methods. The course includes tutor feedback and participant discussion.

Name: Hominin Contemporaries of Early Modern Humans
About Course: For most of our existence as a species, we have shared the world with other kinds of human, including Neanderthals, Denisovans, and Homo naledi. This course explores the diverse range of human species that overlapped, and sometimes even interbred with us.

Name: Inter-culturally Speaking (Online)
About Course: Are we just who we think we are, or are we also who others think we are? Are we born prejudiced? Can we talk of 'national characteristics'? How can we best live together on this planet?

Name: Introducing Mapping, Spatial Data and GIS (Online)
About Course: Investigate the power of maps and spatial data to document and illustrate local and global issues. Learn how to use Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to explore the world around you and share ideas.

Name: Introduction to Philosophy (Online)
About Course: We think we know, but do we? We think we are free, but are we? We think our actions are moral, but are they? What is this reality we take ourselves to live in?  The oldest questions meet the newest technology in this online introduction to philosophy.

Name: Invertebrate Biodiversity and Population Monitoring Methods
About Course: Part-time over five weeks, this tutor-led training course can be taken from anywhere in the world. It will appeal to students and practitioners in conservation management wanting to improve their invertebrate survey skills.

Name: Italian Renaissance Art c.1400-c.1600 (Online)
About Course: From Bellini and Botticelli to tapestry and tableware, the material culture of the Italian Renaissance continues to fascinate us to this day. This course is an opportunity to explore this unique period.

Name: Italian: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This Italian consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Italian: Lower Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This Italian consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Psychopathology: An Introduction
About Course: Exploring the various historical and contemporary models that endeavour to explain the etiology of psychopathology. A holistic and person-centred approach to the conceptualisation and treatment of distress will be considered.

Name: Scholars and Peasants: How Oxford University was Funded, c.1250-1550
About Course: The course will enable participants to enter the world of Medieval and Renaissance Oxford in the great age of college foundation and expansion from c.1250-1550, showing how this was funded by taxation and by development after 1539 of former monastic land.

Name: Social Entrepreneurship (Online)
About Course: Students on this course will gain knowledge about social entrepreneurs, and how to develop creative solutions to address social problems utilising Gandhi's model of 'be the change you wish to see in the world' to make a difference in the lives of others.

Name: Spanish: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This 10-week consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous two terms. It is primarily tailored to meet the needs of students who completed the weekly class, but new students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Spanish: Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This Spanish consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: The Era of New Energy Transition: Geopolitics, Democracy and Conflict
About Course: How will energy transition from fossil fuels to renewables affect “resource curse” phenomenon - replicate its adverse economic and political effects or lead to the more stable, equitable and democratic world?

Name: The Pianists' Workshop - III
About Course: Explore piano repertoire, interpretation and technique in a lively mixture of talks and workshops, in which all students will have regular opportunities to play.  This class is open to players of all levels and students may join the class in any term.

Name: Tracing your British Ancestors in Local History Sources: 1538-2024
About Course: This online course provides an overview of how to trace family history in Britain from the present day to the 16th century using a range of digital and archival sources.

Name: Trollope, Eliot, Dickens and Hardy: Reading Victorian Fiction (Online)
About Course: Madness, hilarity, doubt and devotion are just some of the many aspects of life explored in the huge wealth of Victorian fiction.

Name: Truth in an Age of Disinformation
About Course: 'What is truth?' is a perplexing and elusive question. A good first response is that truth and falsity are properties of what people say or think. But how is what we think related to actual facts? And what caused the recent corrosion of truth?

Name: Writing Dialogue
About Course: Explore writing dialogue for fiction, stage, radio and screen, and write a piece of your own in one of these formats.

Name: Writing Lives (Online)
About Course: Is there a true story that only you can tell? This course is designed to provide you with the skills you need to turn experiences, recollections and real-life phenomena into literary works that are enjoyable and accessible to a wider audience.

Name: A Fight for Liberty? Revolution in Britain, America, and France, 1642-1799
About Course: Why did revolution break out again and again during the tumultuous 17th and 18th centuries? And why did they play such a key role in shaping the very nature of modern western political culture? Explore with us this fascinating topic!

Name: Archaeology and the Antiquarians
About Course: We have much to learn from the antiquarians about ancient sites and archaeological landscapes.  John Aubrey, William Stukeley and Stonehenge and Avebury will be our primary case studies. We also consider and compare other antiquarians and ancient sites.

Name: Architecture on the Tracks: Railway Architecture, 1830s to Today
About Course: Architecture on the Tracks, Railway Architecture from the 1830s to the PresentRailways transformed the world and introduced new kinds of buildings; stations, hotels, viaducts and tunnel portals. We will explore this exciting range of new buildings.

Name: Food Metabolism and Human Well-being
About Course: This course offers a broader understanding of the key roles of food in promoting well-being.  Topics includes the fundamentals of food metabolism, its function in disease prevention, and the critical relevance of hormone regulation in metabolic processes.

Name: German: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This interactive course further develops the participants' language skills and understanding of the culture, society and daily life in the German-speaking countries.

Name: German: Lower Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This German consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Great Moral Issues in Contemporary Society
About Course: An introduction to some great moral issues: animals, abortion, euthanasia, immigration, multiculturalism, freedom of speech and religion, capital punishment, war, world hunger, economic justice. Each week, we'll address an issue and the debate around it.

Name: How else could we organise the economic system?
About Course: Many people hate capitalism and wish to replace it, but what with? This short course considers prominent alternatives to capitalism and how they could work.

Name: Japanese: Lower Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This Japanese consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Korean: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This Korean consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Latin: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This course introduces you to the basic principles of Classical Latin. It provides a firm basis of grammar, sentence structure and vocabulary of the language, through which you will be able to read and translate into English Roman drama in adaptation.

Name: Latin: Lower Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This course introduces you to the basic principles of Classical Latin. It provides a firm basis of grammar, sentence structure and vocabulary of the language, through which you will be able to read and translate into English Roman drama in adaptation.

Name: Marx’s Capital
About Course: Marx's Capital is one of the most famous and consequential books of the last two hundred years. Melding philosophy, political economy, history and more, delivered in a pungent literary style, it remains one of the classic accounts of the modern condition.

Name: Mindfulness and Meditation: The Art and Science of Self-transformation
About Course: Explore the theory and practice of mindfulness/meditation effects within Eastern and Western religious traditions and in a modern therapeutic context. Try out various techniques. Learn about the art and science of meditation, including its controversies.

Name: Musical Literacy
About Course: This course will cover the basics of reading and writing down music and also, the theory that underpins it - notation, rhythm, melody, harmony and form - relating theory to practice with examples from over three centuries of repertoire.

Name: Pandemic Data Science
About Course: Data science is revolutionising our healthcare systems and pandemic preparedness. This course will highlight some of key contributions that data science has made to shaping our response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Name: Portuguese: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This Portuguese consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Prehistoric Art
About Course: The art of prehistoric Europe is rich with imagery such as cave paintings, carvings, body ornamentation and frescoes. This course considers a range of sites and artefacts in our exploration of the unique and creative ways people visualised their world.

Name: Python Programming for Data Science: Introduction
About Course: Gain insight into the most important programming tools using the Python programming language, for obtaining data, bringing it into a usable form, exploring and modelling it, and for presenting discoveries to a wider audience.

Name: Reading Literature Critically
About Course: With an emphasis on close critical analysis, this course is designed to enable you to become a more attentive, appreciative and critical reader of literary texts.

Name: Should we do more for the poor beyond the borders?
About Course: Explore the ethical and economic issues arising from an unequal world with borders. Should we focus more on the poorest in the world and less on our fellow citizens? What are the implications for various policies such as trade, aid, tax and immigration?

Name: The Archaeology of the Classical World: An Introduction
About Course: This introductory course introduces the Classical World through an exploration of the archaeology of the cities, villages, temples and daily lives of two ancient Mediterranean societies: the Greeks and the Romans.

Name: The Political Economy of the End of Human Civilisation
About Course: Climate change will cause agricultural land to turn into deserts. Artificial intelligence will make millions of people out of work. Biotechnology will increase life spans will strain the welfare systems of countries as will mass migration.

Name: The Quantum Universe
About Course: The course covers the development of the notion of quanta, from its origin as a solution to the problem of radiation emission, to its possible ultimate consequence - the quantisation of space and time.

Name: Twisted Columns: The History of Baroque Architecture
About Course: Masses, oval shapes, and twisted columns are features of Baroque architecture. The course retraces its origins and look into the best examples of European and English Baroque from Francesco Borromini, Filippo Juvarta to Christopher Wren and James Gibbs.

Name: A Brief History of Physics from Galileo to the 20th Century and Beyond
About Course: We will look at the epoch-making work of Galileo and how he influenced Newton as well as the toppling of the Aristotelian world view. After Newton, we will look at more classical physicists and conclude with Relativity, Particle and Quantum Physics.

Name: Alan Turing and the Birth of Modern Computing
About Course: Explore Alan Turing's contributions to the foundations of computing including how the Turing Machine - his mathematical model of the computer - helps define basic computational steps and the theoretical limits of computation.

Name: Ancient Greek: Elementary - Consolidation
About Course: This 10-week consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous two terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of students who completed the weekly class, but new students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: British Landscape Painters: Eric Ravilious, John Nash, Gilbert Spencer
About Course: Discover how Ravilious, Nash and Spencer immersed themselves in the British landscape, capturing the essence of the countryside in their artworks.

Name: Political Economy of Taxation
About Course: Taxation affects us all, and people often complain about it, but how can the system be improved? This introductory course for the lay person gives you the tools to analyse and assess potential tax system reforms.

Name: R Programming for Data Science: Introduction
About Course: Learn about R programming with this online course. At an introductory level, this course provides you with a solid foundation of the R programming language. Here you will learn the basics of R and gradually move to data processing and manipulation.

Name: Walking the Past
About Course: There are archaeological sites all around us: hillforts and stone circles, Roman towns, ancient fields and roads. During this course, we will venture out and look at the archaeological landscape.

Name: Espionage, Terrorism and Warfare in the Cyber Age
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Providing an overview of the digital revolution’s impact on international security. The day comprises four lectures that will explore the internet’s evolution, and cyber’s impact on espionage, warfare and terrorism.

Name: Oxford College Gardens
About Course: An exploration of Oxford University’s hidden college gardens, past and present. The college gardens current multifaceted role as a retreat and refuge, as a counterpart to the dense urban grain and as a source of college income will be evaluated.

Name: The Psychology of Happiness
About Course: Searching for happiness has been a major preoccupation through the centuries. Explore the concept of happiness from a psychological perspective at this day event in Oxford.

Name: A History of British and Irish Poetry from Barrett Browning to Paul Muldoon
About Course: Ever wanted to know more about poetry but didn't know where to start? If so, this lively and accessible course is for you. Together, we will close read a selection of poetry from c.1850 to now, from Britain and Ireland, in relation to its wider contexts.

Name: Academic Literacy: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: If you are new to higher education, or have not studied for some time, you may find it useful to brush up your reading, note-making and essay-writing skills, and to revisit the basic rules of punctuation and grammar.

Name: Advanced Coaching
About Course: This course helps any coach deepen their practice in various ways: enhancing intervention skills, better understanding clients' needs, drawing on evidence, exploring attitudes to work/clients, and expanding client bases and professional standing.

Name: Ancient Egypt: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: From royal pyramids, court artisans and powerful pharaohs, to grandiose temples, mysterious gods and foreign invasions, participants will experience the world of ancient Egypt, its highs and lows, and the rich tapestry of its culture.

Name: Ancient Greek: Lower Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: Ancient Greek is the language of Homer, Sophocles, Plato, the New Testament and many other texts. This class is for students who have either completed Ancient Greek 1 or have prior knowledge of Ancient Greek from elsewhere.

Name: Archaeology in Practice (Online)
About Course: How do archaeologists recognise and interpret the lives of past peoples and their societies? An introduction to the methods and techniques of archaeological enquiry, from initial site survey and excavation to scientific analysis.

Name: Artificial Intelligence Concepts: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Aimed at a general audience, including professionals and those with no prior knowledge, this course provides an essential introduction to the key topics underpinning Artificial Intelligence.

Name: Artificial Intelligence Concepts: Practical Applications (Online)
About Course: Understanding the impact of Artificial Intelligence, now and in the future, is a key skill in the knowledge economy. This course develops a critical understanding of real-world AI applications by introducing various case studies to a general audience.

Name: Biblical Studies: The Bible, Its Content and Theology: An Introduction
About Course: Introduction to the content of the Old Testament/Hebrew Bible and the New Testament, together with their religious and socio-political backgrounds, languages and main theological themes and interpretations.

Name: Britain and Its Empire (Online)
About Course: This course examines the rise and fall of the British Empire and its manifold legacies in Britain and beyond.

Name: C++ Programming: Introduction
About Course: C++ will be used to introduce object-oriented programming, commencing at an introductory level. We will move onto encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, software engineering, dynamic data allocation, recursion as well as the standard template library.

Name: Classical Architecture: A Design Workshop
About Course: An introduction to classical design in architecture, its ancient origins, its impact on Oxford architecture and modern examples. To include demonstrations by well-known modern practitioners and the chance for students to create their own designs.

Name: Counselling: An Introduction
About Course: An introduction to the main schools of Counselling and Psychotherapy, as well as to basic counselling skills. Sessions will include presentations and discussions, and skills practice sessions in groups of 2 to 4 people. No previous experience is required.

Name: Dickens
About Course: This course explores the works, life, and contexts of one of English literature's greatest authors.

Name: French: Lower Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This interactive course further develops the participants' language skills and understanding of the culture, society and daily life in the French-speaking countries.

Name: Fundamental Characterisation for Nanotechnology
About Course: This ten-week online course will survey the range of techniques and methodologies used to determine the nature and composition of nanoparticles, thin films and nanostructures. It includes a hands-on visit to Begbroke Science Park over two days.

Name: Italian: Intermediate - Consolidation
About Course: This Italian consolidation course is based on the syllabus of the previous terms and is primarily tailored to meet the needs of those who completed the weekly class. New students who are at the appropriate level of proficiency are also welcome.

Name: Learn to Sing - II
About Course: A practical course for singers who have attended Learn to Sing I or have other singing experience. Singing technique will be discussed and repertoire explored but the course will focus on workshop sessions, working on interpretation and vocal technique.

Name: Macroeconomics: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: This course provides a detailed introduction to, and encompasses the fundamentals of macroeconomics. On completion of the course you will have the ability to critically assess real-world macroeconomic developments at first-year undergraduate level.

Name: Microeconomics: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: This course provides a detailed introduction to microeconomics. On completion of the course, students will have the ability to understand and apply the principles of microeconomics at first-year undergraduate level.

Name: New Testament Hermeneutics: From Christ's Passion to Ascension
About Course: The narrative of the last days of Jesus is a subject of great interest for biblical and theological studies. This course will analyse the main interpretations and meanings given throughout history to a story that still raises many questions.

Name: Psychology: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: This course introduces the science of psychology, exploring the richness of human functions, uncovering the brain's secrets and revealing its complexities. Studies from biological, psychodynamic, cognitive, behavioural and social approaches are presented.

Name: Public Policy Economics (Online)
About Course: All of us are affected by government policies, and governments place particular emphasis on economic policies. This course will equip you to evaluate the economic arguments made about public policy choices.

Name: Reading and Writing Poetry
About Course: This course is for those who have always wanted to write poetry, but have never actually tried, and it will take place within an encouraging and supportive environment.

Name: Statistical Computing for Health Care Research
About Course: This fully online course is designed to complement your statistical skills with expert methods in R

Name: Statistics for Clinical Trials
About Course: Plan, execute and interpret the statistical analysis of clinical trials.

Name: Systematic Reviews
About Course: Covering the process of doing a systematic review, focusing on practicalities and emphasising how and why this qualifies as scientific research.

Name: The History and Evolution of Counselling and Psychotherapy
About Course: Explore the fascinating evolution of psychotherapy from its philosophical roots to modern methods. Engage with key theories, dissect transformative ideas, and prepare to shape future therapeutic practices. Open to all, but great CPD for practitioners!

Name: The Impressionists: Painting Modern Life (Online)
About Course: Examine the major concerns of artists such as Cézanne, Monet, Manet and Degas and their intimate interaction with modern life.

Name: The Wars of The Roses: Power, Politics and Personalities (Online)
About Course: The recent discovery of Richard III's remains in Leicester highlights the dynamic new research being conducted into the period known as the Wars of the Roses. This course asks students to engage with the latest work on this exciting and tumultuous period.

Name: Writing Drama (Online)
About Course: A creative and critical course helping you develop your passion for drama into the craft of dramatic writing.

Name: Geology in the Field
About Course: Develop a practical understanding of geological landscapes in Oxfordshire and adjacent counties. See the rock outcrops and learn techniques for geological fieldwork by visiting geological localities within driving distance of Oxford.

Name: Ancestral Voices: The Earliest English Literature (Online)
