About Course: This course introduces you to Old English literature: from tales of heroism, courage and fellowship, to poignant elegies of love and loss.

Name: Exploring the Universe (Online)
About Course: How old is the universe? How unusual is the Solar System? How will it all end? Oxford astronomers Chris Lintott and Robert Simpson provide an overview of the last 13.7 billion years of cosmic evolution, answering these questions and more.

Name: Henry VIII (Online)
About Course: The reign of Henry VIII transformed British history. This course charts the political, religious and cultural changes of the period.

Name: Jane Austen (Online)
About Course: Many readers enjoy Austen's novels, but what makes them so special and enduring?

Name: Learning to Look at Modern Art (Online)
About Course: This course will seek to provide guidelines about how to look at modern art in an open-minded, critical and analytical way.

Name: Learning to Look at Western Architecture (Online)
About Course: This course is designed to enable you to 'read' the architecture of the Western world in a critically informed way.

Name: Learning to Look at the Visual Arts (Online)
About Course: This course offers you the opportunity to learn how to study and analyse paintings, drawings and prints, and learn the 'language of looking'.

Name: Political Philosophy: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Political philosophy contains some of the greatest writings in the Western intellectual tradition. This online course introduces you to the central questions concerning the state, by means of classical and contemporary texts.

Name: Ritual and Religion in Prehistory (Online)
About Course: How can we begin to understand the spiritual lives of prehistoric people? When do religious ideologies first appear on the human evolutionary timescale? Using both anthropology and archaeological evidence these and many other questions are examined.

Name: Van Eyck to Memling: Northern Renaissance Art c.1430-1480 (Online)
About Course: The work of northern Renaissance artists is often incredibly beautiful, with marvellous colours and textures. But there is much more to their work than simple aesthetics, for it evolved from an intriguing range of religious and cultural beliefs.

Name: Learn to Write Short Stories
About Course: A weekend intensive workshop on the art and craft of writing short stories. We’ll write, read and analyse modern classics and experiment with this versatile narrative form.

Name: Mathematics: An Inclusive Discipline?
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Through centuries and continents, Maths has evolved thanks to the effort and contributions of countless individuals. But is this representative of the variety of the human characters? Is Maths suited for true inclusivity?

Name: The Archaeology of Britain's Changing Coastline
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Discover how Britain’s coastline has changed and evolved over millennia with rising sea levels. Explore submerged landscapes and learn about the risks posed to coastal heritage by climate-driven sea-level rise.

Name: The Impact of Climate Change and Invasive Species on Islands
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Islands often harbour a unique and diverse fauna, but island biodiversity is also very vulnerable to a range of human-created threats. Explore the impact of two of the main threats: climate change and invasive species.

Name: Adverse Drug Reactions, Drug Interactions and Pharmacovigilance
About Course: This course is led by Dr Michael Theodorakis and features lectures and tutorials in epidemiology, systematic reviews and pharmacovigilance.

Name: Artificial Intelligence Concepts: Introduction to Machine Learning (Online)
About Course: Machine Learning methods lie at the heart of the Artificial Intelligence revolution. This course introduces fundamental concepts to explain Machine Learning methods, potential, and pitfalls to a general audience.

Name: Brontës (Online)
About Course: How did three sisters living apparently secluded, eventless lives write such original, passionate and dramatic literature?

Name: Clinical Prediction Rules
About Course: Understanding the principles involved in designing, creating and testing clinical prediction rules.

Name: Course Design, Assessment and Evaluation
About Course: Educational strategies to develop a course and design assessment of learning and evaluation. Part of the Evidence-Based Health Care programme.

Name: Islamic Art and Architecture (Online)
About Course: This course is for anyone interested in understanding Islamic art and culture, and examines the relationship between faith and art forms.

Name: Minoans and Mycenaeans (Online)
About Course: The Minoans and Mycenaeans left us with the intriguing Greek Bronze Age sites of Knossos, Mycenae, Pylos and Akrotiri. The excavation of these sites turned archaeologists into superstars, as stunning architecture, sculpture and weaponry were revealed.

Name: Mixing it up: understanding and using mixed methods research in social sciences
About Course: An online course for researchers which critically discusses mixed methods approaches to social science analysis.

Name: Philosophy of Mind (Online)
About Course: The philosophy of mind is concerned with questions about the nature of mind and the relation between our minds and the physical world. This course provides an introduction to the mind body problem, one of the most intractable problems in philosophy.

Name: Philosophy of Science (Online)
About Course: This course introduces key issues in the philosophy of science, including debates about the nature of the scientific method, theories of confirmation, the demarcation of science from non-science, the rationality of theory change, and scientific realism.

Name: Realist Reviews and Realist Evaluation
About Course: Aiming to provide an understanding of realist reviews and evaluation and the ability to apply new knowledge and skills to a realist research project.

Name: Shakespeare (Online)
About Course: This course focuses on five Shakespeare plays, covering a range of genres and periods of his writing.

Name: Vikings: Raiders, Traders and Settlers (Online)
About Course: Ravagers, despoilers, pagans, the Vikings are often regarded as bloodthirsty pirates. Yet they were also traders, settlers and farmers with a thriving artistic culture and legal systems.  Using archaeology we examine the varied aspects of the Viking world

Name: Writing Fiction (Online)
About Course: This course is for those who would like to write but don't know how; who tried once and gave up; or who already write but would like to improve; and for readers who have no desire to write but want a different perspective on how fiction works.

Name: Writing Fiction for Young Adults (Online)
About Course: Find your own voice and your own niche in writing for young adults, in sub-genres from realism to the supernatural.

Name: Writing Poetry (Online)
About Course: How can poetic form help you to turn the passion and intensity of life into memorable expressions? How can an appreciation of the techniques used by past and living poets help you to improve as a poet? Take this course and find out.

Name: Analysing Classical Music: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: The aim of musical analysis is to understand how music exerts such a powerful effect on us. This course introduces some of the main approaches as we attempt to bridge the gap between our intuitions about music and our intellectual knowledge of it.

Name: Churchill: Soldier, Politician and Statesman (Online)
About Course: Sir Winston Churchill, regarded as one of Britain's greatest statesmen, still provokes controversy and debate. The aim of this course is to study his life in detail, assess his successes and failures and to gain some insights into the complex personality.

Name: Europe of the Dictators (Online)
About Course: Why were the inter-war years a period of such political extremism and dictatorial rule across Europe?

Name: Globalisation (Online)
About Course: Everybody is talking about 'globalisation' - but what does it really mean? What factors drive globalisation and what are the consequences for all of us? How can and should we govern processes of globalisation?

Name: International Labour Migration: Economics, Politics and Ethics (Online)
About Course: This global course analyses one of the most controversial public policy issues of the 21st century: how to regulate international labour migration and the rights of migrant workers.

Name: Politics: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: In addition to tracing the evolution of the modern state and political ideas and ideologies, this course focuses on issues that confront people from all parts of the world on a day-to-day basis.

Name: Social Anthropology: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: Social anthropology is the study of how humans give meaning to the world through different social norms, values, practices and means of organisation. This course provides an exciting and dynamic introduction to the world of social anthropology.

Name: The Architecture of the English Medieval Cathedral (Online)
About Course: This course will explore the English medieval cathedral as a developing institution which survived over a thousand years of religious upheaval and historical change, focusing on the multifaceted architecture of a range of truly great churches.

Name: The First Civilization: Mesopotamia (Online)
About Course: Civilization was born over 5,000 years ago on the fertile plains of southern Mesopotamia.  Using archaeology and textual sources, this course will build a picture of the Sumerian civilization, one that lies at the root of our own world.

Name: The Making of Modern Britain (Online)
About Course: A modern, democratic, multicultural Britain developed throughout the twentieth century. This course will examine the key social, economic and political influences that have shaped modern Britain.

Name: Therapeutic Photography: An Introduction
About Course: Explore photography's power to express emotions and heal wounds. Learn techniques and apply them for mental wellbeing and personal growth. Gain practical experience and insights to use photography for self-development and professional practice.

Name: Veteran Welfare Past and Present
Mode: Online - live- Short courses- Hybrid - in person or online
About Course: Examine the origins of military welfare for veterans and widows during the British Civil Wars of the 1640s, comparing that with the provision provided to service personnel and their families today by the Armed Forces Covenant.

Name: Art Nouveau across Europe (Online)
About Course: From Paris to Moscow, Glasgow to Barcelona, this course examines the richness and variety of European art nouveau.

Name: Bioethics for Beginners (Online)
About Course: Do you think reproductive cloning is morally permissible? Do you check food labels to exclude buying any with GM ingredients? Would you worry if the government introduced compulsory depositing of DNA in the national DNA bank?

Name: Critical Reasoning: A Romp through the Foothills of Logic (Online)
About Course: Reasoning enables us to acquire knowledge, to persuade others and to evaluate their arguments. But only if we reason well. We shall be learning how to recognise, evaluate, construct and analyse arguments, and how to recognise common fallacies.

Name: Ethics: An Introduction (Online)
About Course: In this introduction to ethics, we shall examine four important ethical theories, applying them to two practical questions: the rights of animals and euthanasia. There will be plenty of opportunity to engage in debate and test your own thinking.

Name: Evidence-Based Diagnosis and Screening

Name: English Literature Summer School
About Course: A three-week residential summer school in English literature at Exeter College, with options for both undergraduate- and graduate-level study.

Name: Exploring Psychology: Understanding Human Behaviour

Name: From Edward to Elizabeth: The British Monarchy 1901-2022
About Course: Five British monarchs - Edward VII, George V, Edward VIII, George VI and Elizabeth II - were entrusted with the crown between 1901 - 2022. This course examines their lives and impact on Britain during the 20th and 21st centuries.

Name: Gothic Horror Novels: In the Footsteps of the Monster
About Course: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein; Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights; Robert Louis Stevenson's The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and Oscar Wilde's The Picture of Dorian Gray are stories that haunt the imagination. This course explores why.

Name: History, Politics & Society Summer School
About Course: Gain insight into issues and events that have influenced the contemporary world in this three-week residential summer school.

Name: Impudent Housewives: Debunking Stereotypes of Early Modern Women
About Course: Early modern women were told to ‘stay home and meddle with your housewifery’, but many of them did not. This course will explore the ways that women at all levels of society across England were politically active, intelligent, and influential.

Name: In Search of Time: The Art and Science of the Fourth Dimension
About Course: The eternal fascination of artists, scientists, film-makers and writers alike, we explore  the myriad manifestations of humankind’s engagement with time, from scratches on stone to the Theory of Relativity, from art-house cinema to the metaphysical novel.

Name: Italian Renaissance Art: Does it Matter?
About Course: Examine the major revolution in the arts that took place in the period called Italian Renaissance, by looking at works by key artists from Cennino to Michelangelo, and encompassing architecture, sculpture, paintings, drawings, manuals and treatises.

Name: Laughter and Redemption: The Genres and Modes of Comedy
About Course: Spanning several thousand years of European and anglophone drama, novels and film, this course searches for an answer to the questions 'why are comedies enjoyable?' and 'why do we laugh?'

Name: Lights, Camera, Action! - British Cinema in the 21st Century
About Course: Examining how British cinema has evolved in the 21st Century, delve into production, distribution, and exhibition sectors. Learn how Cinema, a lens for cultural and social issues, reflects historical and contemporary national identity shifts.

Name: Macroeconomics: Keynes and the Monetarists
About Course: Covid-19 has generated an environment for a potential global economic crisis. During these uncertain times, the economic ideas of John Maynard Keynes have become more and more relevant to policymakers than those who believe in a totally free market.

Name: Queenship in Early-Modern Britain
About Course: How far did the gender of Mary I, Elizabeth I, and Mary, Queen of Scots, influence their queenship? Using written and visual sources, we shall consider the impact of sixteenth-century attitudes to women on the early lives and reigns of these three queens.

Name: Scandal, Satire, Sensibility: 18th-Century Women Novelists
About Course: Exploring the fascinating lives and novels of 18th-century women who defied public opinion and family pressure to write and publish fiction for enjoyment, money, and fame: Eliza Haywood, Frances Burney, Ann Radcliffe, Charlotte Lennox, and Maria Edgeworth

Name: Shakespeare's Kings: Villain or Hero?
About Course: Richard III and Henry V are two of Shakespeare’s most famous historical plays. Dazzling and dangerous, Shakespeare’s Richard III is a theatrical and historical ‘villain’. In creating Henry V, Shakespeare weaves heroic myths around ‘this star of England’.

Name: The Happy Healthy Cell
About Course: This course will introduce some of the main cellular structures, and their function in human cells. We will explore how the normal “happy” cell maintains a healthy body, concluding with a discussion about advances in cell biology.

Name: Women of Power in the Tudor and Stuart World
About Course: The lives of women in the early modern world are often assumed to have been narrow and restricted. This course will use textual, visual, and material sources to reveal more about the lives and experiences of women, ranging from noblewomen to laundresses.

Name: Writing Fiction: Getting Started with your Novel
About Course: Many feel that we have a book in us. A short and inspirational course, ideal for getting started. Together we will gather your ideas and plans, and by systematically working through the basics of fiction, learn tools to shape them into your novel.

Name: Clinical Translation and the Commercialisation of Nanomedicine
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: This five-day course provides an overview of the regulatory, financial, clinical and commercial challenges faced by those wishing to bring innovative nanotechnologies to market.

Name: Satellite Connectivity and Navigation: Systems, Services and Market
Mode: Short intensive- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: A thorough overview of satellite connectivity and navigation where we investigate the technical, financial and business aspects linking market requirements to technical capabilities whilst considering the crucial aspects of costs and financing.

Name: The History and Philosophy of Evidence-Based Health Care
About Course: Critical thinking about the assumptions of the health care profession, and learning about the empirical foundations of science

Name: 17th-Century Dutch and Flemish Art: Rubens to Rembrandt to Vermeer
About Course: Embark on a journey through 17th-century Dutch and Flemish art: Van Dyck &  Rubens for grandeur, Hals & Lester for the elevation of the everyday, Rembrandt's  penetrating self-portraits, or Vermeer's seducing Girl with the Pearl Earring.

Name: Capitalism, Socialism, and/or Democracy
About Course: Is capitalism better than socialism? How do we decide? Can democracy thrive under either, or both? How do bureaucracy and technocracy fit in? We will try to answer these questions by looking at the political economy of several countries.

Name: Colleges of Oxford
About Course: Through illustrated talks and walks on foot around Oxford we shall explore the history and architecture of Oxford, and in particular the extraordinary group of historic colleges of the University that date from the 13th to the 21st century.

Name: Forest and Flood: The Natural World in the Middle Ages
About Course: Responses to the natural world are everywhere in the literature and art of the Middle Ages. We will explore bestiaries, the forests of romance, the landscapes of dream vision and the calendar pages of Books of Hours.

Name: Introduction to Classical Music
About Course: “Classical” music comes in an enormous range of styles and national traditions, spanning hundreds of years. We will explore music in a (mostly) non-technical way, aiming to give listeners a deeper sense of understanding and involvement in the music.

Name: King Arthur: From the Middle Ages to the Modern Day
About Course: Who was King Arthur, what is his place in British culture, and why have we spent more than 1,000 years telling stories about him? We will explore the literature and significance of the Arthurian legend, from the Middle Ages through to the present.

Name: Leonardo da Vinci: Art and Knowledge
About Course: This course will look at Leonardo da Vinci’s paintings, drawings and notebooks within the interdisciplinary framework of art and science. It will offer a viewing of key drawings in Oxford collections.

Name: Medieval Heresy and Dissent, 300-1500
About Course: Examine religious heresy and dissent through time, from rival strands of Christianity in the later Roman world, to the dualist Catharism that flourished in S France and N Italy c.1150-1250 and late medieval English heresy’s connection to Oxford.

Name: Pirates, Adventurers and Fortune-seekers
About Course: This course joins the explorers and adventurers of the Elizabethan and Jacobean periods who looked beyond England towards new territories and new opportunities, in the process making discoveries which fundamentally changed the world in which they lived.

Name: Savage Country: Humanity’s Changing Relationship to the Idea of Wilderness
About Course: “Wilderness” often describes natural areas that seem untouched by humans. We will examine this controversial idea and debates about wilderness in a time of environmental crisis, through history, literature, philosophy, painting, and photography.

Name: Scientific Breakthroughs of the 20th Century
About Course: DNA, quantum mechanics, relativity, plate tectonics, radio communications and computing. Emphasising historical context, this course offers detailed appraisals of the startling intellectual and technical 20th century achievements forged in peace and war.

Name: Seamus Heaney: The Oxford Years
About Course: The course will focus on Heaney’s highly accessible collection, Seeing Things (1991), written during his tenure as Oxford Professor of Poetry. As his lectures reflect his responses to diverse range of poets, we will also look at samples of their poetry.

Name: Shakespeare's Tragic Worlds
About Course: Hamlet and Antony and Cleopatra show the breathtaking range of Shakespeare’s tragedies. Hamlet’s world is grief-stricken, claustrophobic and murderous. Explore the tragic intersections of romantic passion and imperial ambitions in Antony and Cleopatra.

Name: Telling Right from Wrong: An Introduction to Ethics
About Course: Should you be a moral person and concerned about others’ well-being, or is it okay to be selfish? Does being a moral person mean following moral principles? What tells you what actions are morally right: reason, emotions, intuitions or your society?

Name: The Eternal Alexander the Great: Reality, Myth, Legacy
About Course: This course focuses on the founder of the greatest empire the ancient world had ever seen, Alexander the Great, who has been an example to European and Islamic rulers and remains the hero of numerous legends and stories worldwide.

Name: The Gender of Diplomacy
About Course: We will cover historical roles, women's participation, global impact of gender policies, and future trends in diplomacy. Includes interactive sessions and expert insights ideal for diplomacy, Gender, equality of representation and our changing world.

Name: The Making of England: Anglo-Saxons, Vikings and Normans
About Course: An introduction to the archaeology and history of England from the 5th century to the early 12th century, covering Anglo-Saxon England; the Viking raids and the establishment of the Danelaw; the Norman Conquest; the Domesday Book and Norman England.

Name: The Untold Cold War: Stories Beyond the Superpowers
About Course: Challenging traditional narratives that understand the Cold War through ‘East vs. West’ paradigms, our course examines the Cold War through alternative prisms with stories that changed the directions of this ideological and geopolitical struggle.

Name: The World on a Page: An Introduction to Writing Flash Fiction
About Course: Flash fiction is defined as complete stories told in 1000 words or fewer. Join us for a week of writing, learning, experimenting and honing your writerly craft - and discover why flash is the ideal genre for beginners and seasoned writers alike.

Name: Writing Fiction: Getting Started with your Novel
About Course: Many feel that we have a book in us. A short and inspirational course, ideal for getting started. Together we will gather your ideas and plans, and by systematically working through the basics of fiction, learn tools to shape them into your novel.

Name: “Written in my life-blood”: J.R.R. Tolkien and The Lord of the Rings
About Course: An appreciation and critical appraisal of what is often called one of the great novels of the twentieth century. This course will look at the concepts, themes, inspirations, and continuing legacy of Tolkien’s The Lord of the Rings.

Name: High Impact Supply Chain Management
About Course: This course has been specifically designed for Supply Chain Managers who are developing into broader SCM leadership roles, and Executives with responsibility for SCM in their organisations.

Name: 1000 Years of the English Garden
About Course: This course will look at the evolution of the English garden from the Norman conquest of 1066 to the present day and at the people and ideas which have influenced that evolution, from monastic and castle gardens to everyone's garden in a democratic age.

Name: A Voyage of Discovery: The Trans-Siberian Railway
About Course: The Trans-Siberian Railway spans 6,000 miles and 9 time zones but also the 2,000 years of Russia's complex and little understood history. Through the windows of our railway carriage we get an insight into this enduringly mysterious country and its people.

Name: Brushstrokes Through Time: Celebrating 200 Years of the National Gallery
About Course: 2024 marks the 200th birthday of the National Gallery, London, a temple of Early  Modern European art. Explore the themes of tradition and innovation from the Renaissance to  the 19th/20th centuries (Leonardo, Turner, Van Gogh, Cézanne etc).

Name: Creative Writing For All
About Course: A practical and discursive creative writing course which encourages students to use their own life experience as a springboard for the creation of original fiction. Absolute beginners and practising writers are equally welcome.

Name: Digital Diplomacy: Adapting to our Modern World
About Course: A week exploring Digital Diplomacy: covers evolution, social media use, ethical challenges, and future trends, with case studies and expert insights. Ideal for all interested in diplomacy, technology and our changing world.

Name: Enigma and the Intelligence War
About Course: In World War II the secret government Code and Cipher School was based at Bletchley Park. The course offers a historic and archival analysis and evaluation of the work of Station X in decrypting German Enigma signals intelligence during the War.

Name: Greek Myths: Poetry, History, Politics, Psychology
About Course: Fascinating stories with their intriguing mix of strangeness and familiarity. What could they possibly mean? Why were they created? How can we explain their power to inspire writers, dramatists and painters for millennia?

Name: How to Write a Stage Play
About Course: A workshop-based course exploring the key skills required to create an original and compelling stage drama, with reference to current creative practice in new writing in professional theatres.

Name: International Security in the Cyber Era
About Course: This course delivers an overview of the digital revolution’s impact on international security. We will explore espionage, terrorism, and warfare to understand these disciplines in the cyber era.

Name: Lewis Carroll's Oxford and the Surprising Histories of Alice's Wonderland
About Course: Learn why, 150 years later, Alice is still so fascinating to us. This course will explore the real origins of Lewis Carroll’s Alice’s in Wonderland, its hidden histories and kaleidoscopic afterlife.

Name: Modernist Literature Through Oxford and London
About Course: This course uses the cities of London and Oxford to introduce key figures in modernist literature. How can the streets and buildings of London and Oxford help us understand the work of Virginia Woolf, T.S. Eliot, Wyndham Lewis and Dorothy Sayers?

Name: Myths and Legends of the British Isles: from King Arthur to Jerusalem
About Course: The rich tradition of legendary history in the British Isles has provided fertile ground for writers and film makers. We’ll explore these ancient stories and the ways in which they have been reimagined in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries.

Name: Opera in the Age of Bel Canto
About Course: Bel canto simply means beautiful singing but the expression is particularly associated with the operas of Rossini, Donizetti, Bellini and early Verdi.  This course looks at their major works, and the roots of their music in the Italian vocal tradition.

Name: The Dark Triad: Psychology of Narcissism, Machiavellianism and Psychopathy
About Course: The Dark Triad- Narcissistic, Machiavellian, Psychopathy- a very specific set of personality traits. Few people would desire or express such traits however they are often seen in leading roles in many areas.

Name: The Rise and Fall of the British Empire
About Course: This course explores the rise and fall of the British Empire: the greatest empire the world has ever seen. It had a tremendous impact on the history of the world and its effects are still felt today in numerous nations, including in the United Kingdom.

Name: The World of the Vikings
About Course: Although often regarded as bloodthirsty pirates, the Vikings were also traders, settlers and farmers with a highly developed artistic culture and legal system. This course will use recent findings from archaeology to examine the Viking world.

Name: Three Outsiders: Pissarro, Caillebotte, Toulouse-Lautrec
About Course: Camille Pissarro, Gustave Caillebotte and Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec were all outsiders in 19th century France. Each left us with a unique body of exceptional Impressionist artworks, some of which are held in Oxford’s own Ashmolean Museum.

Name: Writing the World: The Travel Writer at Home and Abroad
About Course: Travel writing faces an uncertain future in a world shrunk by instability & climate change, but stories are still there to be told, some of them close to home. Through readings, discussion & writing exercises, students will achieve insight in this genre.

Name: Digital ethnography
About Course: Explore issues and methods involved in conducting qualitative and/or ethnographic research in the social sciences related to the digital with this online course.

Name: Adventures in British Popular Music 1965-2000
About Course: Enjoy the popular music of ten central British acts, such as the Who, Pink Floyd, Led Zeppelin, the Smiths, the Police, Kate Bush, and Radiohead. We will look at what made their music individual, and related changes in music technology and song-writing.

Name: Bright Young Things: Oxford and the Brideshead Generation
About Course: Why has the Oxford of Brideshead Revisited, and the ‘Bright Young Things’ who epitomized it, maintained such a grip on our imagination? Through the words, images, and lives of varied yet interconnected Oxford writers, we will explore their vibrant world.

Name: Creative Writing Summer School
About Course: Develop your creative writing skills in this three-week residential summer school at Exeter College, Oxford. For aspiring and experienced writers.

Name: Creative Writing for All
About Course: A practical and discursive creative writing course which encourages students to use their own life experience as a springboard for the creation of original fiction. Absolute beginners and practising writers are equally welcome.

Name: English Language Teachers' Summer Seminar
Mode: Summer schools- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: A two-week summer programme designed for teachers of English as a Second Language with more than four years' experience, presented as a series of practical workshops.

Name: Four Queens of Crime
About Course: A study of the four queens of crime, Sayers, Marsh, Allingham and Christie, all of whom wrote murder mysteries in the Golden Age of crime fiction between the wars and have enduring popularity today.

Name: Geopolitics: Finding the Patterns in the Chaos
About Course: International politics has rarely been so interconnected and impactful on our lives, yet can often seem beyond comprehension. This course will show the patterns in the chaos, as together we navigate the choppy waters of geopolitics today.

Name: Introduction to Modernism
About Course: What is ‘Modernism’? How did writers in the early 20th century - from James Joyce and Virginia Woolf to TS Eliot and HD - ‘make it new’? This lively course will read a selection of poetry and prose to explore an experimental, daring period of literature.

Name: Lives Across Borders: Introduction to Migration and Diasporas
About Course: This course focuses on migration and the broad range of transnational experiences migrants may have when negotiating their belonging to home and host countries, roles in diaspora communities, and connectedness to compatriots around the world.

Name: Saints and Sinners: The Renaissance Papacy 1450-1550
About Course: Renaissance popes were monarchs who accumulated spiritual, political and cultural power. This course examines how the Curia worked to increase papal authority and considers the dynastic, cultural and political significance of the main Renaissance popes.

Name: The Cotswolds: Past, Present and Future
About Course: An introduction to the historical, geographical, social and political realities and traditions of the Oxfordshire Cotswolds, so quintessentially English.

Name: The Twelve Caesars: Emperors of Rome
About Course: The extraordinary lives of the rulers of Imperial Rome and the actions of their wives. History gives vivid accounts of the often scandalous but always fascinating events in the lives of these emperors. Can we distinguish between ‘fact’ and propaganda?

Name: Who Am I? Notions of Selfhood in Western and Eastern Thought
About Course: What, if anything, distinguishes us from other living creatures on this planet? Are we essentially immaterial minds or just bundles of genes? Will technological progress eventually reshape human nature and change our collective identity as a species?

Name: Art Glass, Glass Artists: Craftsmen, Chemists, Visionaries
About Course: Glass: one of the oldest and most extraordinary of man-made materials. Our course explores glass and the arts of working it from Antiquity to the present day; the discovery and rediscovery of techniques and the achievements of its greatest practitioners.

Name: Bismarck to Merkel - The Search for German Identity
About Course: Between 1865 and 1945 Germany made the proud but painful transition from political non-entity to failed superpower. Post-war Germans might have become demoralised by defeat. Instead they reinvented themselves as a different but hugely influential nation.

Name: Human Diversity: An Introduction to Anthropology
About Course: What makes us human and what are the characteristics that connect us cross-culturally in this experience? We will tackle the questions that have kept anthropologists engaged since the birth of the discipline and try ourselves in the role of ethnographers.

Name: International Politics Summer School
About Course: Tackle the vital issues that shape politics in the modern world in this two-week residential summer school.

Name: Memoir: Begin Writing your Life
About Course: Everyone has an interesting life story, and this course will enable you to present your own.  In this practical course we shall learn about the pattern of ourselves so that we may present it to others.

Name: Muses of Fire: The Medieval World in Shakespeare’s Plays
About Course: He is the great playwright of the English Renaissance. So why Medieval Shakespeare? This course takes a fresh look at some of Shakespeare’s best-known plays by discussing the influence of the medieval worldview and the rich traditions of medieval drama.

Name: Royal Pretenders and Imposters
About Course: Before DNA testing, how did a person prove their blood-right to a throne? Pretenders and imposters flourished at times of turmoil, often used as tools by their country’s enemies. This course examines examples from the 14th century to the 20th century.

Name: Social and Cultural History of the People of Britain
About Course: This course will examine the social and cultural history of people living in Britain from the eighteenth to the early twentieth century, examining the transformation of identity, community and belonging.

Name: The Architecture and Archaeology of Medieval Churches
About Course: A practical introduction to understanding the history and development of medieval churches.

Name: The Beatles, Popular Music and Sixties Britain
About Course: Learn how the Beatles made their music, and trace its development from simple first recordings to the multi-track of Abbey Road in the context of examples of Top 30 charts of the era, poetry, journalism, photographs, film and key cultural events.

Name: The Hundred Years War
About Course: The course investigates the causes and consequences of medieval Europe’s longest war.

Name: The Oxford Murder: Crime Fiction in Oxford
About Course: Why is the city of dreaming spires also the city of murders? Oxford is the setting for more fictional murder mysteries than any other city, featuring amateur and police detectives from Wimsey to Morse and beyond.

Name: Zen Buddhism and the West: A Philosophical Odyssey
About Course: What is Zen? Why did it become popular in the West? From the Buddha to Japan and North America, we explore the origin, content, development, flourishing and influence of Zen via engagement with various philosophical themes and problems.

Name: An Introduction to Tolkien's Mythology
About Course: A masterclass in world-building and the meaning of 'The Silmarillion', led by a world-class Tolkien expert, at the university where Middle-earth was created.

Name: Beyond the Pages: The Brontës in Context
About Course: Charlotte, Emily and Anne Brontë wrote some of the most distinctive and celebrated fiction of the early nineteenth century. This course explores how they navigated themes such as the supernatural, religion, female empowerment and sexual desire.

Name: Cardinal Wolsey: Christ Church Patron and Renaissance Prelate
About Course: The course examines the life and career of England's 'Renaissance Cardinal', Thomas Wolsey, founder of Oxford's Cardinal College, now Christ Church.

Name: Culture & Conversation - How to Navigate Intercultural Communication
About Course: This course provides practical tools on how to efficiently communicate across the widest variety of cultural settings, with our focus areas being intercultural communication skills in translation, business and advertising.

Name: High Performance Leadership: Arts to Sports
About Course: igh Performance Leadership - the ability to perform at the highest level consistently, repeatably and for long periods of time. Looking at a diverse range of fields, how do the very best leaders manage to do that? What tools and strategies do they use?

Name: Keep on Creative Writing
About Course: This creative writing course is for writers of all levels of experience and is suitable for anyone who has a desire to get their stories down onto the page, and out into the world.

Name: Lewis Carroll's Oxford and the Surprising Histories of Alice's Wonderland
About Course: Learn why, 150 years later, Alice is still so fascinating to us. This course will explore the real origins of Lewis Carroll’s Alice’s in Wonderland, its hidden histories and kaleidoscopic afterlife.

Name: Living in a Material World: Artefacts, Archaeology and British History
About Course: Cultural artefacts hold stories of histories and people through their material world, in the past, the present and perhaps toward the future. This course takes an archaeological approach, examining British history through its rich and diverse artefacts.

Name: Mini Masterpieces: Prose Poetry, Micro-Memoir, Flash Fiction and More
About Course: This fast-paced, hands-on week gives you a chance to try your hand at four popular and distinct forms of writing: prose poetry, micro-memoir, flash fiction and flash creative non-fiction.

Name: Queens Regnant in Great Britain
About Course: This course asks why there were no queens regnant in England or Scotland before Mary Queen of Scots, and then delves into the lives and reigns of some of the best-known and most colourful rulers in British history.

Name: Romantic Moderns: The Arts and the Imagination in Britain 1927-51
About Course: Explore the imaginative character of mid-20th century British Neo-Romanticism, including the writings of Virginia Woolf and Dylan Thomas; the art of Piper, Nash, and Ravilious; and the music of Ralph Vaughan Williams.

Name: Shakespeare and the Spirits of the Age: Magic, Witchcraft and the Fantastical
About Course: From witches on a blasted heath to magicians on a magical island, magic and the fantastical pervades Shakespeare’s work. This course examines both their dramatic effect, and what they tell us about our human condition.

Name: The Age of Winston Churchill
About Course: Explore the massive changes in Britain in the 20th century through Winston Churchill's career as a political radical, chronicler, anti-totalitarianism and war leader from Victorian times to the Cold War.

Name: The Bayeux Tapestry: An Early Medieval Masterpiece
About Course: The Bayeux Tapestry is the greatest surviving artefact from the Anglo-Norman era, portraying the Norman Conquest of England in 1066 in pictorial form. This course examines its provenance, sponsorship, interpretation, and intriguing later history.

Name: The Black Death and the Transformation of Medieval England
About Course: The Black Death of 1348-9 is widely acknowledged to be one of the great historical turning points. This course explores the impact of plague on later-medieval English society, and includes a field trip to a deserted medieval village.

Name: The Devil You Know: Dissecting Criminology and Christian Theology
About Course: The nature of evil and suffering has haunted humankind since time immemorial. This course takes a walk through some of the best and lesser-known bad guys in Scripture and asks where, and how, bad people and Christian theology meet.

Name: The Jewel in the Crown: The British Raj in India
About Course: This course will examine the political, economic, and socio-cultural experience of the British Empire by focusing on 'the Jewel in the Crown' - the British Raj in India.

Name: The Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood
About Course: Explore the Victorian Rebellion of the Pre-Raphaelites in Oxford, home to several masterpieces of the Brotherhood. Millais, Rossetti, Hunt & Burne-Jones infused modernity to the establishment being inspired by the past and by the complexities of love.

Name: Theology Summer School
Mode: Summer schools- Short courses- Professional development
About Course: A two-week residential summer school for members of the clergy, theologians and teachers of religious education. Held at Christ Church.

Name: Thomas Hardy's Novels and Poetry: Men, Women and Tragedy
About Course: The Victorian author Thomas Hardy was sensitive to the patterns of the past and to the tragic inevitabilities of human nature.  By studying his poetry and prose, this course examines Hardy’s philosophy and belief in the roles of men and women.

Name: Understanding the Cosmos
About Course: An introduction to all things cosmological. From the birth of stars to the death of black holes, from Relativity to quantum mechanics and the Big Bang, we examine humankind’s most astounding discoveries and the most challenging questions facing science.

Name: Ancient Art: From Cave Paintings to Celtic Imagery
About Course: From cave paintings, carvings, colourways and ornamentation, studying ancient art offers tantalising insight into past societies. This course takes an archaeological and art historical approach, following a fascinating journey through European prehistory.

Name: Conquistadors and the Age of Discovery
About Course: This course examines Spanish explorers during the age of discovery. A motley crew of adventurers, better known as Conquistadors, whose greed drove them to cross the seas in search of riches and fame.

Name: Country Houses
About Course: The country house has been described as England's most distinctive contribution to European culture. This course will examine the growth of the country house phenomenon from the Middle Ages, up to the present day.

Name: Exploring Alien Worlds
About Course: We will boldly go on a voyage of discovery through our solar system, as well as the planetary systems of other stars. Learn about space exploration, planetary science, and the perennial search for habitable planets and extra-terrestrial life.

Name: Introduction to Criminology and Forensic Psychology
About Course: Fascinated with the psychology of serial killers, sex offenders and stalkers? Gripped by the social, familial and environmental reasons for crime? Then join us an enthralling dive into the hearts and minds of killers, conmen and predators.

Name: Post-Impressionism: Van Gogh, Gauguin, Cézanne
About Course: Indulge in the art of the Post-Impressionists: the focus on Vincent van Gogh, Gauguin and Cézanne. Other Post-Impressionists will also be considered such as Seurat or Toulouse-Lautrec.

Name: Quantum and Relativity: The Science of Reality
About Course: A layperson’s guide to contemporary science’s most strange and startling frontiers, quantum physics and relativity. In tandem with a variety of historical, philosophical and every-day contexts we explore both fields in plain, non-mathematical language.

Name: Rethinking Human Nature
About Course: What if anything distinguishes us from other living creatures on this planet? Are we immaterial minds or best understood as bundles of genes? Will technological progress eventually reshape human nature and change our collective identity as a species?

Name: The Brontës: Landscape, Nature and the Unnatural
About Course: How did three sisters living apparently secluded, eventless lives write such original, passionate and dramatic literature? This course investigates the inspiration for their remarkable fiction and memorable protagonists.

Name: The Making of the Oxfordshire Landscape
About Course: This course opens up the historical  development of rural Oxfordshire beyond the ‘dreaming spires’. We explore centuries of collaboration and conflict to understand the county’s changing landscape from its medieval foundations to 1850.

Name: The Medieval Monasteries of Oxford
About Course: During the Middle Ages, Oxford was home not only to a great university but also to many monasteries, nunneries, priories, and friaries. This course will examine their buildings, history, and legacy.

Name: Tolkien and C.S. Lewis in Oxford
About Course: Explore the work and friendship of the men behind Middle-earth and Narnia in the contexts of Oxford, their Inklings circle, and their insights into our own world - ancient and modern.
